STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.speaker: IK, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.claim: Most cited commentators prefer to read 2:204–7 as universal teaching on hypocrisy, despite reports of specific incidents.
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.anchor: most prefer to see these verses as universal teachings on the nature of hypocrisy (IK, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:205/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r1.claim: Turning away may mean becoming angry or simply leaving the presence of those one is deceiving.
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r1.anchor: Turns away can refer to becoming angry or more generally to leaving the presence of those one is deceiving (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:205/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r2.claim: Some say the verse describes a particular hypocrite who burned fields and hamstrung a donkey.
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r2.anchor: According to some this verse describes a particular hypocrite who burned some people’s fields and hamstrung their donkey

STUDYQURAN:2:205/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r3.anchor: The tillage refers to crops and agriculture

STUDYQURAN:2:205/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r4.speaker: IK, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r4.claim: Offspring may mean livestock, or more broadly any offspring including human beings.
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r4.anchor: the offspring refers to livestock, though some commentators say it can mean any offspring, including human ones (IK, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:205/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r5.claim: Fasād literally means rot and here broadly covers corruption, decadence, and immorality.
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r5.anchor: literally “rot,” is used here, as in most instances in the Quran, to mean corruption

STUDYQURAN:2:205/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r6.speaker: some Muslims
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r6.claim: Some Muslims also apply earthly corruption to social injustice and environmental destruction.
STUDYQURAN:2:205/r6.anchor: Such verses about the corruption of the earth are interpreted by some Muslims to also be referring to injustice in society and also to the destruction of the natural environment

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says 2:204 concerns al-Akhnas b. Shurayq, who professed Islam and swore sincerity to the Prophet, then burned Muslim crops and killed their donkeys, prompting 2:205.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.anchor: عن السدي " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that hypocrites mocked the Muslims killed at al-Rajīʿ as having died pointlessly; the verses contrast their hypocrisy and corruption with the martyrs’ reward and those who give themselves for God.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال " لما أصيبت هذه السرية أصحاب خبيب بالرجيع بين مكة، والمدينة، فقال رجال من المنافقين

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.claim: A second transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās’s al-Rajīʿ account names ʿĀṣim and Marthad among the expedition and says the report otherwise matches the preceding version.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة مولى ابن عباس أو عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال: «لما أصيبت السرية التي كان فيها عاصم، ومرثد، بالرجيع

TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.speaker: سعيد المقبري
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.claim: Saʿīd al-Maqburī quotes a scripture describing people with honey-sweet tongues, bitter hearts, and soft outward manners who pursue worldly gain through religion; God threatens a trial that will bewilder the wise.
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.anchor: سمعت سعيدا المقبري يذاكر محمد بن كعب، فقال سعيد

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ describes a servant whose speech is good but deeds are bad: he speaks pleasingly to the Messenger, then leaves to cause corruption.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.speaker: عامة القراء
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.claim: The majority reading makes the hypocrite call God as witness that his profession agrees with his belief in God and His Messenger, although he lies.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.anchor: فقرأته عامة القراء: {ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه}

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes tawallā as the hypocrite turning away and leaving Muhammad; he then works forbidden corruption in the land, such as cutting roads and terrorizing travelers.
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r1.anchor: فمعنى الآية: وإذا خرج هذا المنافق من عندك يا محمد غضبان عمل في الأرض بما حرم الله عليه

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the hypocrite’s turning away as leaving the Prophet’s presence.
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وإذا تولى} [البقرة: 205] قال: يعني: وإذا خرج من عندك سعى

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says tawallā here means becoming angry.

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r4.claim: Saʿā means to work or act; al-Aʿshā’s line about Kinda uses it for laboring on their behalf in commendable deeds.
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r4.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى: [البحر الكامل] وسعى لكندة سعي

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله " {وإذا تولى سعى} [البقرة: 205] قال: عمل

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r6.claim: The author says the hypocrite acts in God’s land through sin and corruption; the verse does not restrict this to one kind of wrongdoing.
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r6.anchor: عمل في الأرض بما حرم الله عليه، وحاول فيها معصية الله، وقطع الطريق، وإفساد السبيل على عباد الله

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r7.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r7.claim: One reported explanation takes the corruption as cutting roads and frightening travelers, as in the earlier account of al-Akhnas.
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: تأويله ما قلنا فيه من قطعه الطريق، وإخافته السبيل

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the corruption is severing kinship and spilling Muslim blood; when challenged, the wrongdoer claims he is seeking nearness to God.
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج، في قوله: " {سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها} [البقرة: 205] قطع الرحم، وسفك الدماء

TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r9.claim: All sins count as corruption, so the phrase is not limited to one offense; road banditry and terror best fit the context linking corruption with destruction of crops and offspring, though other corruption is possible.
TAB-FULL:v3p580#2/r9.anchor: غير أن الأشبه بظاهر التنزيل أن يكون كان يقطع الطريق، ويخيف السبيل، لأن الله تعالى ذكره وصفه في سياق الآية

TAB-FULL:v3p583/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says al-Akhnas destroyed the harvest by burning Muslim crops and destroyed offspring by killing their donkeys.
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r1.anchor: «كان ذلك منه إحراقا لزرع قوم من المسلمين، وعقرا لحمرهم» حدثني بذلك، موسى بن هارون، قال: ثني عمرو بن حماد، قال: ثنا أسباط، عن السدي

TAB-FULL:v3p583/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r2.claim: Mujāhid says aggression and injustice cause rain to be withheld, destroying crops and offspring; citing 30:41, he explains “sea” as any village beside flowing water, not only the sea proper.
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها ويهلك الحرث والنسل} [البقرة: 205] الآية

TAB-FULL:v3p583/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī glosses al-ḥarth as crops, al-nasl as descendants and offspring, and destruction of crops as burning them.
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r3.anchor: وأما الحرث، فإنه الزرع، والنسل: العقب، والولد وإهلاكه الزرع: إحراقه

TAB-FULL:v3p583/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r4.claim: The author allows that crops may also perish when their caretakers are killed, offspring may cease when parents are killed, and rain may be withheld because of sin, though direct burning and killing fit the wording best.
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r4.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون كان بقتله القوام به، والمتعاهدين له حتى فسد فهلك

TAB-FULL:v3p583/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r5.claim: Although Mujāhid’s drought explanation is possible, al-Ṭabarī prefers al-Suddī’s direct reading as the closer fit to the apparent wording.
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r5.anchor: فإن الذي هو أشبه بظاهر التنزيل من التأويل ما ذكرنا عن السدي، فلذلك اخترناه

TAB-FULL:v3p583/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī generalizes the threat to unjust killing of any animal, whether killing it is never lawful or would be lawful only in some circumstances; the verse does not restrict the category.
TAB-FULL:v3p583/r6.anchor: لأن الله تبارك وتعالى لم يخصص من ذلك شيئا دون شيء بل عمه

TAB-FULL:v3p586/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-ḥarth as what people cultivate and al-nasl as the offspring of every animal; another transmission adds human beings as well.
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r1.anchor: قال: الحرث: حرثكم، والنسل: نسل كل دابة

TAB-FULL:v3p586/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r2.claim: Mujāhid says al-ḥarth is the vegetation of the earth and al-nasl is every walking creature, including people and animals.
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {ويهلك الحرث} [البقرة: 205] قال: نبات الأرض

TAB-FULL:v3p586/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the harvest as plants of the earth and offspring as the progeny of every kind of thing.
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: " {ويهلك الحرث} [البقرة: 205] قال: نبات الأرض

TAB-FULL:v3p586/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the harvest is vegetation and offspring means the progeny of every animal.
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، قال: " الحرث. النبات، والنسل: نسل كل دابة

TAB-FULL:v3p586/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r5.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r5.claim: Al-Rabīʿ identifies the harvest as crops people cultivate and offspring as the progeny of every animal.
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r5.anchor: عن الربيع: {ويهلك الحرث} [البقرة: 205] قال: " الحرث الذي يحرثه الناس

TAB-FULL:v3p586/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r6.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the harvest is crops and offspring includes people and livestock, whose young may be killed.
TAB-FULL:v3p586/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قلت لعطاء: " {ويهلك الحرث والنسل} [البقرة: 205] قال: الحرث: الزرع

TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r1.claim: Mujāhid again explains destruction of the harvest as destruction of plants and offspring as destruction of animals generally.
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: " يبتغي في الأرض هلاك الحرث: نبات الأرض، والنسل: من كل شيء من الحيوان

TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says al-ḥarth is the origin and al-nasl means every animal, including people.
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {ويهلك الحرث والنسل} [البقرة: 205] قال: الحرث: الأصل، والنسل: كل دابة

TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r3.speaker: مكحول
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r3.claim: Makhūl glosses al-ḥarth as what people cultivate and al-nasl as the offspring of everything.
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r3.anchor: قال مكحول: " الحرث: ما تحرثون، وأما النسل: فنسل كل شيء

TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r4.speaker: بعض القراء
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r4.claim: Some readers put yuhliku in the nominative, coordinating it with yashhadu and making it describe the person who pleases the listener and then destroys crops and offspring.
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r4.anchor: وقد قرأ بعض القراء: (ويهلك الحرث والنسل) برفع «يهلك» على معنى

TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the nominative reading despite its grammatical possibility because it conflicts with the readers’ consensus; Ubayy’s codex has li-yuhika, supporting the accusative coordinated with li-yufsida.
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r5.anchor: وذلك قراءة عندي غير جائزة وإن كان لها مخرج في العربية لمخالفتها لما عليه الحجة مجمعة من القراءة

TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r6.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb’s reading in his codex, “li-yufsida fīhā wa-li-yuhika,” supports reading yuhika in the accusative as coordinated with li-yufsida.
TAB-FULL:v3p586#2/r6.anchor: وأن ذلك في قراءة أبي بن كعب، ومصحفه فيما ذكر لنا: ليفسد فيها وليهلك الحرث والنسل

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.claim: These verses classify people by hypocrisy versus sincerity in faith, whereas the preceding verses classify them by whether they seek this world or the next; the connection to the Hajj verses is clear.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.anchor: تشتمل الآيات على تقسيم آخر للناس من حيث نتائج صفاتهم، كما أن الآيات السابقة

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r7.claim: Tawallā means taking authority and power; the next verse supports this, since the man’s worldly standing is acquired through sin and hypocrisy hidden beneath his speech.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r7.anchor: ويؤيده قوله تعالى في الآية التالية { أخذته العزة بالإثم }

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r8.claim: Another possible sense is turning away from the conversation: after leaving, he changes from professed concern for good to pursuing corruption.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r8.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون التولي بمعنى الإعراض عن المخاطبة والمواجهة، أي إذا خرج من عندك كانت

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r9.claim: Destroying crops and offspring explains earthly corruption: human survival depends on food and reproduction, and plants sustain both people and animals, so their ruin destroys humanity.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r9.anchor: ولما كان قوام النوع الإنساني من حيث الحياة والبقاء بالتغذي والتوليد فهما الركنان القويمان

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r10.claim: The disfavored corruption is not natural becoming and decay: the created order entails change, death, and life together, so God cannot hate what He decrees.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r10.anchor: المراد بالفساد ليس ما هو فساد في الكون والوجود الفساد التكويني فإن النشأة نشأة الكون والفساد

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r1.claim: The corruption God rejects is corruption under religious law: revelation reforms deeds and character, bringing balance and happiness to human society in this life and the next.
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r1.anchor: وإنما هو الفساد المتعلق بالتشريع فإن الله إنما شرع ما شرعه من الدين ليصلح به أعمال عباده

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r2.claim: The hypocrite’s apparent reform masks corruption: he distorts words, changes divine rulings, and alters religious teaching, damaging morals, unity, religion, humanity, and worldly life.
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r2.anchor: يفسد بما ظاهره الإصلاح بتحريف الكلمة عن موضعها، وتغيير حكم الله عما هو عليه

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r3.claim: History bears out the passage in rulers whose handling of religion and worldly affairs harmed religion, lowered Muslims, and divided the community; destruction begins with religion and follows with humanity.
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r3.anchor: وقد صدق هذه الآيات ما جرى عليه التاريخ من ولاية رجال وركوبهم اكتاف هذه الأمة الإسلامية

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r4.claim: Some narrations, to be discussed later, interpret the ruined crops and progeny as religion and humanity.
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r4.anchor: ولهذا فسر قوله ويهلك الحرث والنسل في بعض الروايات بهلاك الدين والإنسانية كما سيأتي

TABRISI:2:204-205/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r5.claim: Tawallī means turning away or moving from something toward its opposite.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r5.anchor: والتولي هو الانحراف والزوال عن الشيء إلى خلاف جهته

TABRISI:2:204-205/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r6.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:2:204-205/r6.claim: Saʿā can mean to act or to hurry; al-Aʿshā's line uses it for working on behalf of Kinda.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r6.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
وسعى لكندة سعي غير مواكل

TABRISI:2:204-205/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r7.claim: Fasād is causing harm without entitlement or any legitimate benefit.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r7.anchor: والإفساد: هو عمل الضرر بغير استحقاق ولا وجه من وجوه المصلحة

TABRISI:2:204-205/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r8.claim: Ihlāk removes the possibility of benefit; ḥarth means crops and nasl means offspring.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r8.anchor: والإهلاك العمل الذي ينفي الانتفاع والحرث الزرع

TABRISI:2:204-205/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:2:204-205/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk broadens the terms: ḥarth means every plant and nasl every living creature.

TABRISI:2:204-205/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r10.claim: Nasl evokes emergence or falling away: it describes camel hair or bird feathers shedding, and humanity is Adam's progeny because people emerged from his back.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r10.anchor: ويقال نسل ينسل نسولا إذا خرج فسقط ومنه نسل وبر البعير أو ريش الطائر

TABRISI:2:204-205/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r11.claim: The lām in li-yufsida governs an implicit an, which may be made explicit; unlike 3:179, its lām is not an emphatic mark of negation.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r11.anchor: نصب بإضمار أن ويجوز إظهارها بأن يقال لأن يفسد فيها

TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the three verses were revealed about a hypocritical pretender who outwardly displays what he inwardly opposes.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت الآيات الثلاثة في المرائي

TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.claim: A report from al-Ṣādiq also identifies the verses' referent as a particular person, without naming him here.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.anchor: وهو المروي عن الصادق ع إلا أنه عين المعني به

TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verses were revealed about the hypocrites generally.

TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the referent as al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who displayed affection for the Prophet and Islam while concealing the opposite.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق وكان يظهر الجميل بالنبي

TABRISI:2:204-205/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r21.claim: One explanation is that he turns away from what is good.

TABRISI:2:204-205/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r22.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:2:204-205/r22.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes tawallā as gaining authority and becoming a governor.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r22.anchor: ملك الأمر وصار واليا عن الضحاك

TABRISI:2:204-205/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r23.speaker: ابن جريج
TABRISI:2:204-205/r23.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes it as turning away from the promise he had made in his speech.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r23.anchor: ولي عن قوله الذي أعطاه عن أبن جريج

TABRISI:2:204-205/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r24.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r24.claim: He hurries away from Muhammad, or the phrase means that he works on earth.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r24.anchor: أي أسرع في المشي من عندك وقيل عمل في الأرض

TABRISI:2:204-205/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r25.speaker: ابن جريج
TABRISI:2:204-205/r25.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the corruption as severing kinship and spilling blood.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r25.anchor: ليقطع الرحم ويسفك الدماء عن ابن جريج

TABRISI:2:204-205/r26.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r26.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r26.claim: Another explanation is that he spreads corruption and commits acts of disobedience.

TABRISI:2:204-205/r27.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r27.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r27.claim: The threatened destruction is of crops and children.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r27.anchor: أي النبات والأولاد وذكر الأزهري أن الحرث النساء

TABRISI:2:204-205/r28.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r28.speaker: الأزهري
TABRISI:2:204-205/r28.claim: Al-Azharī says ḥarth can mean women and nasl their children, connecting the image to 2:223.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r28.anchor: وذكر الأزهري أن الحرث النساء والنسل الأولاد لقوله

TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r1.speaker: الأزهري
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r1.claim: The verse 2:223 calls wives a field, supporting al-Azharī's gloss of ḥarth as women.
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r1.anchor: نساؤكم حرث لكم [البقرة: 223] وروي عن الصادق ع

TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r2.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṣādiq interprets ḥarth here as religion and nasl as people.
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع إن الحرث في الموضع الذين والنسل الناس

TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r3.claim: The rejected corruption may mean corrupt action or, in another explanation, corrupt people.
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r3.anchor: أي العمل بالفساد وقيل أهل الفساد

TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r4.claim: The verse refutes the Mujabbira: God's love is His will, so His denial of love for corruption means He does not will corruption.
TABRISI:2:204-205#2/r4.anchor: وفيه دلالة على بطلان قول المجبرة إن الله تعالى يريد القبائح لأنه تعالى نفى عن نفسه محبة الفساد

THALABI:v2p119#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p119#2/r2.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v2p119#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says al-Akhnas passed Muslim fields and donkeys, burned the crops, and hamstrung the animals.
THALABI:v2p119#2/r2.anchor: قال السدي: مر بزرع للمسلمين وحمر فأحرق الزرع وعقر الحمر.

THALABI:v2p119#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p119#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v2p119#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says al-Akhnas went to Taif to collect a debt, burned the debtor's land, and hamstrung his she-camel; this prompted the verses.
THALABI:v2p119#2/r3.anchor: مقاتل: خرج إلى [الطائف] مقتضيا حلاله على غريم

THALABI:v2p120/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p120/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p120/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say verses through Allah's compassion to servants concern the Raji expedition: Quraysh lured six Muslims with a false conversion request, ambushed them, killed three, and captured Khubayb and Zayd.
THALABI:v2p120/r1.anchor: ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت هذه الآيات إلى قوله والله رؤف بالعباد في سرية [الرجيع]

THALABI:v2p120/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p120/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p120/r2.claim: In the Raji account, Aasim fought until captured; bees protected his corpse, then rain and a flood carried it away, fulfilling his vow never to touch or be touched by a polytheist. Umar marveled at God's protection.
THALABI:v2p120/r2.anchor: ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت هذه الآيات إلى قوله والله رؤف بالعباد في سرية [الرجيع]

THALABI:v2p122/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r18.claim: The phrase means that he turned away and departed from the Prophet.

THALABI:v2p122/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r19.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p122/r19.claim: Al-Hasan says he turned away from the promise he had made.
THALABI:v2p122/r19.anchor: الحسن: تولى عن قوله الذي أعطاه.

THALABI:v2p122/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r20.speaker: ابن جريح
THALABI:v2p122/r20.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets تولى as becoming angry.
THALABI:v2p122/r20.anchor: الحسن: تولى عن قوله الذي أعطاه. ابن جريح: غضب.

THALABI:v2p122/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r21.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v2p122/r21.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets it as taking control and becoming governor.

THALABI:v2p122/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r22.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r22.claim: سعى means he worked or acted in the land; Arabic also uses it for working to provide for one's family, as al-A'sha's line about Kinda and Qays illustrates.
THALABI:v2p122/r22.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى: وسعى لكندة سعي غير مواكل

THALABI:v2p122/r23.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r23.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p122/r23.claim: Another explanation takes سعى as traveling or walking.

THALABI:v2p123/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r1.speaker: ابن جريح
THALABI:v2p123/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains corruption here as breaking kinship ties and shedding Muslim blood.
THALABI:v2p123/r1.anchor: قال ابن جريح: قطع الرحم وسفك دماء المسلمين

THALABI:v2p123/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p123/r2.claim: فساد is a general name for every kind of sin.

THALABI:v2p123/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق
THALABI:v2p123/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Abi Ishaq read يهلك with a nominative kaf, as the start of a new clause.
THALABI:v2p123/r3.anchor: قرأ الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق: ويهلك برفع الكاف على الابتداء

THALABI:v2p123/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r4.speaker: العامة
THALABI:v2p123/r4.claim: The common reading has the accusative; Ubayy's reading وليهلك supports it by making destruction purposive and coordinated.
THALABI:v2p123/r4.anchor: وقرأت العامة: بالنصب، ويصدقها قراءة أبي: وليهلك.

THALABI:v2p123/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r5.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v2p123/r5.claim: The commentators gloss الحرث as cultivated plants and النسل as offspring of every animal, including humans.
THALABI:v2p123/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: الحرث ما تحرثون من النبات، والنسل نسل كل دابة والناس منهم.

THALABI:v2p123/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p123/r6.claim: Mujahid says that when the man turned away, fear made him act unjustly; God then withheld rain and destroyed crops and offspring.
THALABI:v2p123/r6.anchor: النضر بن عدي عن مجاهد في قوله وإذا تولى سعى الآية قال: إذا ولى خاف

THALABI:v2p123/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v2p123/r7.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib says clipping a dirham is corruption on earth.
THALABI:v2p123/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: قطع الدرهم من الفساد في الأرض.

THALABI:v2p123/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r8.speaker: قتادة وعطاء
THALABI:v2p123/r8.claim: Qatada reports asking Ata about a man in ihram wearing a robe: the Prophet ordered him to remove it; Ata answered that God does not love corruption when Qatada suggested it be torn.
THALABI:v2p123/r8.anchor: قتادة عن عطاء: إن رجلا يقال له العلاء بن منبه أحرم في جبة فأمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ينزعها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes his turning away as returning to Mecca: after leaving Badr with Banu Zuhra, al-Akhnas attacked Thaqif by night, killed their livestock, and burned their crops.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {وإذا تولى} يريد: راجعا إلى مكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r2.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r2.claim: Al-Suddi gives another incident: al-Akhnas passed a Muslim field and donkeys, burned the field, and hamstrung the donkeys.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r2.anchor: وقال السدي. مر بزرع للمسلمين وحمر، فأحرق الزرع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r3.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and Mujahid read tawalla as gaining authority: when he governs, he acts unjustly; Ibn Abbas instead takes it as departing and turning away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬5) ومجاهد (¬6): تولى بمعنى: ملك وولي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r4.claim: Most exegetes take the harvest as crops and plants and the progeny as livestock offspring, consistent with the report that he destroyed animals and burned crops.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r4.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن المراد بالحرث: الزرع والنبات، وبالنسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r5.claim: Mujahid says that when a ruler acts through aggression and injustice, God withholds rain, so the drought destroys crops and livestock offspring.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إذا ولي فعمل بالعدوان والظلم أمسك الله المطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes the harvest as women and offspring as children; the author says this is soundly possible, citing the description of wives as a field.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن الحرث: النساء، والنسل: الأولاد، وهذا غير مدفوع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r7.claim: Nasl means offspring; its root may denote something emerging and falling out, as feathers, camel hair, or donkey hair shed, and a fallen piece is nusala.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r7.anchor: والنسل: معناه في اللغة: الولد، يقال: نسل بولد كثير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r8.claim: The verb yansilun in the verse about people rushing to their Lord means hastening out; nasl is offspring because it emerges from the father's back and mother's womb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p76/r8.anchor: ومنه قوله عز وجل: {إلى ربهم ينسلون} [يس: 51]، أي: يسرعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r1.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in al-Kalbi's transmission, explains that God does not approve corruption or sinful acts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي: أي: لا يرضى بالفساد والعمل بالمعاصي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r2.claim: Corruption here has been glossed as ruin, clipping a coin, or tearing clothes when there is no beneficial purpose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r2.anchor: وذكر في تفسير الفساد هاهنا: الخراب، وقطع الدرهم، وشق الثياب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r3.claim: The verb and verbal noun vary as fasada/fasudan or fasadan, paralleling dhahaba/dhuhuban or dhahaban and kasada/kusudan or kasadan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p78/r3.anchor: ويقال: فسد الشيء يفسد فسودا وفسادا، كما يقال: ذهب ذهوبا وذهابا

QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.claim: Qashani quotes a saying: give sinners glad tidings that God forgives, and warn the righteous that God forgives.
QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.anchor: بشر المذنبين بأني غفور وأنذر الصديقين بأني غفور

QASHANI:2:204-205/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:204-205/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:204-205/r3.claim: When he turns away, he spreads corruption through permissiveness and heresy, as Qashani says is seen among many claimants to love and unity.
QASHANI:2:204-205/r3.anchor: لإباحته وتزندقه كما ترى عليه أكثر مدعي المحبة والتوحيد

QASHANI:2:204-205/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:204-205/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:204-205/r4.claim: His claim to love God is false: a lover does what the beloved loves, but God does not love his corrupt actions; Qashani supports the point with an unnamed poet's couplet about disobedience contradicting love.
QASHANI:2:204-205/r4.anchor: وكيف تتأتى له والمحب لا يفعل إلا ما يحب محبوبه، والله لا يحب ما يفعله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r1.claim: After returning to Mecca, he passed a Muslim's crops and donkeys, burned the crops, and hamstrung the animals.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r1.anchor: { وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض... } الآية، وذلك أنه رجع إلى مكة، فمر بزرع وحمر للمسلمين، فأحرق الزرع وعقر الحمر،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r2.claim: The offspring meant are animal offspring.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r2.anchor: فهو قوله: { ويهلك الحرث والنسل } أي: نسل الدواب.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r15.claim: Here tawalla can mean either that he departs from the Prophet or that he takes charge of an affair.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r15.anchor: Senden ayrılınca veya bir iş başına geçince

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r16.claim: He roams the land to spread corruption and destroy crops and offspring; God neither loves nor approves corruption.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r16.anchor: yeryüzünde fesad çıkarmak ve ekinleri, zürriyetleri mahvetmek için koşar dolaşır {وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْفَسَادَ} Allah da fesâdı sevmez, fesâda râzı olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.claim: The verses were revealed about Ahnes ibn Sharik of Banu Thaqif, an ally of Banu Zuhra, who professed Islam and love to the Prophet, then burned a Muslim field and killed livestock after leaving.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.anchor: Bu âyetler, Benî Sakîf’ten Ahnes b. Şerîk hakkında nâzil olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.speaker: müfessirînin ekser-i muhakkikīni
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.claim: Most authoritative exegetes say the passage applies generally to all hypocrites who display these traits, not only its specific occasion.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.anchor: mazmûn-ı âyet bu gibi evsâf ile muttasıf olan münafıkların hepsine şâmil olduğunu müfessirînin ekser-i muhakkikīni tasrih etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.claim: The passage teaches that people considered for positions of responsibility should be assessed by their conduct, not merely their words.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.anchor: insanların dillerine bakılmayıp hâllerinin tedkīki lüzûmunu iş‘âr için nâstan üçüncü bir kısmın hisâlini göstermiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.claim: One human type speaks attractively but has evil intent and acts as a corrupter and destroyer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.anchor: Bunlardan biri güzel sözlü fakat kötü niyetli, bozguncu ve yıkıcıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.claim: Reports connect the revelation to hypocrites who appeared friendly before the Prophet and acted destructively behind his back.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.anchor: Bazı münafıkların Hz. Peygamber’in yanında dost gibi gözüküp arkasından yıkıcı hareketlerde bulunmaları üzerine bu âyetlerin indiği yolunda rivayetler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.claim: Razi says the verses censure bad qualities rather than particular people, so anyone bearing those qualities deserves censure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.anchor: Râzî’nin de belirttiği gibi Allah Teâlâ bir topluluğu, bazı kötü niteliklerini göstererek yerdiğinde, bundan o kişilerin zatını değil niteliklerini yerdiği anlamı çıkar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.claim: Even if the verses originally concerned one or several hypocrites in the Prophet’s time, their warning applies to everyone who adopts hypocrisy, ostentation, corruption, or destruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.anchor: bu âyetler Hz. Peygamber dönemindeki belli bir veya birkaç münafık hakkında inmiş olsa bile münafıklık, riyakârlık, bozgunculuk, tahripçilik gibi kötü huy ve davranışlar konusunda bütün insanlar için bir uyarı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r7.claim: The phrase is rendered here as taking power, though it can also mean leaving the addressee’s presence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r7.anchor: “Hâkimiyeti ele aldığında...” diye tercüme ettiğimiz 205. âyetteki ifade, “senin yanından ayrılıp gittiğinde...” şeklinde de anlaşılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.claim: Hypocritical and ostentatious people flatter others and invoke God as witness, then after leaving or gaining office act from enmity and damage livelihoods and descendants.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.anchor: Riyakâr veya münafık tabiatlı kişiler genellikle insanın yanında hoşa gidecek sözler söyler, sözlerinin doğruluğuna Allah’ı şahit bile koşarlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r9.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r9.claim: Abduh reads “destroying crops and offspring” as a metaphor for imposing severe hardships on people to satisfy selfish desires and passions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r9.anchor: Muhammed Abduh’un yorumuna göre buradaki “ürünleri ve nesilleri yok etme” ifadesi bir deyim olup bununla kötülerin, bencil isteklerini ve tutkularını tatmin etmek uğruna insanları her türlü ağır sıkıntılar içine sokmaları kastedilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r10.claim: Reading the phrase as taking power also makes the passage a warning about duplicitous politicians who present themselves as peaceful and just, then ruin incomes and corrupt descendants after taking office.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r10.anchor: Aynı bölümü “hâkimiyeti ele alma” mânasında yorumladığımızda söz konusu âyetler ikiyüzlü ve aldatıcı siyasetçilere karşı uyarı anlamı da taşımaktadır

BURHAN:v2p152/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p152/r3.speaker: الروافض
BURHAN:v2p152/r3.claim: The author says interpreting the corrupter in this verse as Muawiya is a false, sectarian allegory.

BURHAN:v2p152/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p152/r4.speaker: أبو القاسم محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري
BURHAN:v2p152/r4.claim: Al-Naysaburi denounces contemporary pretended exegetes for ignorance of recitation and meaning, sensationalism for public favor, and seeking worldly gain without study.
BURHAN:v2p152/r4.anchor: قال الإمام أبو القاسم محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري رحمه الله وقد نبغ في زماننا مفسرون لو سئلوا عن الفرق بين التفسير والتأويل ما اهتدوا اليه

BURHAN:v2p152/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p152/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BURHAN:v2p152/r5.claim: A Prophetic report likens someone claiming what they were not given to wearing two garments of falsehood; no grading is supplied.
BURHAN:v2p152/r5.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم المتشبع بما لم يعط كلابس ثوبي زور

BURHAN:v2p152/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p152/r6.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p152/r6.claim: An unattributed poem warns that pretension to qualities one lacks is exposed by tests and defeated in the race.
BURHAN:v2p152/r6.anchor: وقد قيل … من تحلى بغير ماهو فيه … فضحته شواهد الامتحان

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the hypocritical speaker as al-Akhnas ibn Shariq: after professing sincerity to Muhammad, he burned Muslim crops and hamstrung their donkeys, prompting the next verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.anchor: قال السدي نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي، وهو حليف بني زهرة

DAMGHANI:v1p121/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p121/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p121/r10.claim: Ḥarth means crops or cultivation here; the source groups this with other literal references to fields and crops.
DAMGHANI:v1p121/r10.anchor: وقال تعالى فيها " ويهلك الحرث والنسل " يعني الزرع نظيرها في سورة الأنبياء " إذ يحكمان في الحرث "

DAMGHANI:v1p477/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r4.claim: Halāk can mean corruption: in 2:205 it means ruining crops and offspring, while in 90:6 the speaker means he wasted much wealth.
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r4.anchor: ويهلك الحرث والنسل بمعنى ويفسد وقال تعالى في سورة البلد يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا يعني أفسدت مالا كثيرا

DAMGHANI:v1p357/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p357/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p357/r7.claim: Fasād can mean ruin caused by oppression and injustice; Dāmghānī applies this sense to the phrase that God does not love corruption.
DAMGHANI:v1p357/r7.anchor: ان الملوك اذا دخلوا قرية افسدوها يعني خربوها وفي سورة البقرة والله لا يحب الفساد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r1.claim: One listed sense is refusal, illustrated by people who turn away from migration or from the revealed judgment.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r1.anchor: في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r2.claim: A third sense is turning away, as in several commands and descriptions of people who refuse the Prophet's message.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r2.anchor: والثالث : الإعراض ، ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r3.claim: A fourth sense is fleeing in battle, illustrated by commands against turning one's back and reports of defeated forces.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r3.anchor: والرابع : الهزيمة ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنفال

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r4.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r4.claim: Some add a fifth sense, authority or becoming a ruler; al-Dahhak and Mujahid gloss the verse as becoming a governor over the land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r4.anchor: وهو الولاية ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj are also reported to interpret the verse's tawalla as becoming angry.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس ، وابن جريج ، أن معنى تولى : غضب .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r6.speaker: مقاتل وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p215/r6.claim: Some, including Muqatil and Ibn Qutayba, place this usage under the separate sense of departing or turning away.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r1.claim: Fasad is the verbal noun of becoming corrupt; it means a change from soundness and may describe an object while it remains, when it is undone, or when it vanishes.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r1.anchor: والفساد : تغير عما كان عليه من الصلاح . وقد يقال في الشيء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r2.claim: Corruption can occur in religion through disobedience or disbelief; the entry also distinguishes invalid worship, contracts, testimony, claims, speech, and actions by their legal or practical defects.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r2.anchor: الفساد في الدين كما يذكر في الذات . فتارة يكون بالعصيان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r3.claim: Some invalid rites, such as Hajj and Umrah, must still be completed, whereas an invalid prayer is not continued; contracts are corrupt when legal conditions are unmet.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r3.anchor: ومن العبادات ما يلزم المضي في فاسدها ، كالحج والعمرة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r4.claim: The entry calls testimony corrupt when it should not ground a judgment, a claim corrupt when it is not heard, speech corrupt when disordered, and acts corrupt when they are not credited.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r4.anchor: وفي الشهادة ، إذا لم يجب الحكم بها . وفي الدعاوي إذا لم تسمع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r5.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is disobedience, as in the hypocrites' prohibition against spreading corruption in the land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفساد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r6.claim: The second sense is destruction: if there were gods besides God in the heavens and earth, both would be ruined.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفساد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r7.claim: The third sense is drought and diminished vegetation, as in the appearance of corruption on land and sea.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r7.anchor: والثالث : قحط المطر ( وقلة النبات ) . ومنه قوله تعالى في الروم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r8.claim: The fourth sense is killing: Pharaoh feared Moses and his people would kill Egypt's people; Gog and Magog are called corrupt because they kill people, as is Pharaoh's feared outcome in Ghafir.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r8.anchor: والرابع : القتل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r9.claim: A fifth sense is ruin, applied to the land-corrupting plot in this verse and to conquerors who ruin a town.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r9.anchor: والخامس : الخراب . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r10.claim: The sixth sense is disbelief, in the call for people of understanding to forbid corruption in the land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r10.anchor: والسادس : الكفر . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r11.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r11.claim: The seventh sense is sorcery, as in Moses's statement that God does not make the work of sorcerers succeed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p469/r11.anchor: والسابع : السحر . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r1.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r1.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah defines harth as land made workable for planting; it also names the first track of a horse and the length reached by seed or furrow.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله رحمه الله الحرث اسم لكل ما ذللته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r2.claim: Ibn Faris says harth means gathering; Harith is named from it, and the saying about cultivating for worldly life means working for it as if one would live forever.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r2.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : الحرث : الجمع . وبه سمي الرجل حارثا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r3.claim: The entry also uses harth for a wife as the man's planting ground for children and says to 'cultivate the Qur'an' means to recite it often.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r3.anchor: والمرأة : حرث الرجل . لأنها مزدرع ولده ويقولون أحرث القرآن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r4.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is reward, as in the one who seeks the harvest of the Hereafter receiving more of it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحرث في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r5.claim: The second sense is cultivated land, in verses about cattle churning the soil and the destruction of crops and offspring.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحرث في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p237/r6.claim: The third sense is the place where children are conceived, in the address comparing wives to a field.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r1.claim: Halak and fasad are close in meaning: corruption occurs while the object remains, whereas destruction can occur whether it remains or is gone; the terms overlap in death, annihilation, invalidated proof, and disabled benefits.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r1.anchor: الهلاك والفساد يتقاربان . إلا أن الفساد يكون مع بقاء العين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r2.claim: The first Qur'anic sense of halak is death, including the death of people in a town and the declaration that all things perish save God's face.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الهلاك في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r3.claim: The second sense is punishment, in passages about punished towns and peoples, including the generations with finer possessions and appearance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r3.anchor: والثاني : العذاب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحجر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r4.claim: The third sense is misguidance or loss: 'my authority perished from me' means that my proof was lost.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r4.anchor: والثالث : الضلال . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحاقة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r5.claim: The fourth sense is corruption, as in destroying crops and offspring or wasting a great amount of wealth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p639/r5.anchor: والرابع : الفساد . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

FARRA:v1p123/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p123/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p123/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers the accusative coordination of yuhlika; the nominative is possible if linked instead to the earlier ‘whose speech pleases you, and he destroys.’
FARRA:v1p123/r2.anchor: ومنهم من يرفع «ويهلك» رفع لا يرده على «ليفسد» ولكنه يجعله مردودا على قوله: «ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله- ويهلك» والوجه الأول أحسن.

FARRA:v1p123/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p123/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p123/r3.claim: Arabic has the verbal noun fasūd alongside fasād, just as dhuhūb occurs alongside dhahāb and kasūd alongside kasād.
FARRA:v1p123/r3.anchor: من العرب من يقول: فسد الشيء فسودا، مثل قولهم: ذهب ذهوبا وذهابا، وكسد كسودا وكسادا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r1.claim: When the person turns away, he has departed from the Prophet.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r1.anchor:
{وإذا تولى} أي فارقك.
{سعى في الأرض} أي: أسرع فيها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r2.claim: Saʿā here means to hurry through the land.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r3.claim: The destroyed ḥarth is cultivated crop or planting.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r4.claim: Nasl refers to animals; the person burns, kills, and wrecks things.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#4/r4.anchor: {والنسل} يريد الحيوان. أي يحرق ويقتل ويخرب.

NAHHAS:v1p299/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p299/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p299/r1.claim: Yufsid is subjunctive after the purpose lām, and yuhlik is coordinated with it.
NAHHAS:v1p299/r1.anchor: منصوب بلام كي ( ويهلك الحرث والنسل ) عطف عليه

NAHHAS:v1p299/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p299/r2.speaker: أبي
NAHHAS:v1p299/r2.claim: Ubayy’s reading adds purpose lām before yuhlik, with al-ḥarth and al-nasl accusative.

NAHHAS:v1p299/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p299/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
NAHHAS:v1p299/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read yahluku in the indicative; proposed links are to yuʿjibuka, to saʿā (meaning “strives and destroys”), or an implied huwa.
NAHHAS:v1p299/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة ( ويهلك ) بالرفع وفي رفعه أقوال يكون معطوفا على يعجبك

NAHHAS:v1p299/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p299/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v1p299/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim coordinates the raised verb with saʿā, understood as “he strives and destroys.”
NAHHAS:v1p299/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم هو معطوف على سعى لأن معناه يسعى ويهلك

NAHHAS:v1p299/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p299/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p299/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq supplies an omitted huwa: “he destroys.”
NAHHAS:v1p299/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق التقدير هو يهلك أي يقدر هذا وروي عن ابن كثير

NAHHAS:v1p299/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p299/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
NAHHAS:v1p299/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr is reported to read yahluku with open yāʾ, raising al-ḥarth and al-nasl as its subjects.
NAHHAS:v1p299/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن كثير أنه قرأ ( ويهلك الحرث والنسل ) بفتح الياء وضم الكاف

SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r1.claim: The conditional clause may coordinate with yuʿjibuka, making it part of man’s relative or adjectival clause, or may begin a fresh report after the sentence about aladdu al-khiṣām.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r1.anchor: وهذه الجملة الشرطية تحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن تكون عطفا على ما قبلها وهو " يعجبك "

SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r2.claim: Taken literally, tawallā and saʿā mean that he turns away physically and walks with his feet.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r2.anchor: والتولي والسعي يحتملان الحقيقة أي: تولى ببدنه عنك وسعى بقدميه،

SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r3.claim: Taken metaphorically, tawallā is turning back from his earlier words and saʿā is work and earning; the author cites Q 53:39 and poems by Imruʾ al-Qays and an unnamed poet.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r3.anchor: والمجاز بأن يريد بالتولي الرجوع عن القول الأول، وبالسعي العمل والكسب من السعاية،

SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r4.claim: Saʿāya may also mean harmful speech that divides friends; an unattributed poem describes tale-bearers moving between companions like an enemy.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205/r4.anchor: والسعاية بالقول ما يقتضي التفريق بين الأخلاء، قال: 899 ما قلت ما قال وشاة سعوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r1.claim: Fī al-arḍ modifies saʿā; though one might think walking is necessarily on earth, the phrase generalizes the scope: wherever he settles, he corrupts, so a general setting implies general corruption.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { في الأرض } " متعلق ب " سعى " ، فإن قيل: معلوم أن السعي لا يكون إلا في الأرض قيل: لأنه يفيد العموم،

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r2.claim: The purpose lām in li-yufsida attaches to saʿā and explains its aim.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r2.anchor: و " ليفسد " متعلق ب " سعى " علة له.

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r3.claim: The majority read yuhliku as active causative from ahlaka, with al-ḥarth as object and the verb coordinated with li-yufsida; فساد already entails destruction, so crops and offspring are singled out, as in Q 2:98.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r3.anchor: الجمهور على: " يهلك " بضم الياء وكسر اللام ونصب الكاف. " الحرث " مفعول به،

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r4.speaker: أبي
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r4.claim: Ubayy reads wa-li-yuhlika with an explicit purpose lām, which has the same sense as the majority reading.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبي: " وليهلك " بإظهار لام العلة وهي معنى قراءة الجمهور،

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r5.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, also reported from Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, reads yahliku from intransitive halaka, with al-ḥarth as subject and al-nasl coordinated to it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة - ورويت عن ابن كثير وأبي عمرو - " ويهلك الحرث والنسل " بفتح الياء وكسر اللام

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r6.speaker: قوم
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r6.claim: A group reads the causative yuhliku with the verb in the indicative; it may coordinate with yuʿjibuka, with saʿā as a future sense, an implied huwa, or a fresh sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ قوم: " ويهلك الحرث " من أهلك، و " الحرث " مفعول به إلا أنهم رفعوا الكاف. وخرجت على أربعة أوجه:

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb passively and raises al-ḥarth as its deputy subject.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " ويهلك " مبنيا للمفعول، " الحرث " رفعا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan also reads yahliku with fatḥa on yāʾ and lām and an indicative ending, making al-ḥarth the subject; the open imperfect vowel is rare because neither radical is guttural, as in rakana/yarkan.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ أيضا: " ويهلك " بفتح الياء واللام ورفع الكاف، " الحرث " رفعا على الفاعلية،

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r9.claim: Al-nasl is the verbal noun of nasala, to come out quickly, as camel hair or a bird's feathers shed; another view stresses successive emergence. Imruʾ al-Qays's tan-salu witnesses the sense, and Q 21:96 may fit either.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r9.anchor: والنسل: مصدر نسل ينسل أي: خرج بسرعة، ومنه: نسل وبر البعير، ونسل ريش الطائر

SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r10.claim: Al-ḥarth and al-nasl are verbal nouns by origin but function here as direct objects.
SAMIN-DURR:2:205#2/r10.anchor: و " الحرث والنسل " وإن كانا في الأصل مصدرين فإنهما هنا واقعان موقع المفعول به.

ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r1.claim: Li-yufsida is accusative after an understood an, meaning in order to corrupt; wa-yuhlika may be coordinated with it or begin a new clause with an omitted huwa.
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r1.anchor: نصب (ليفسد) على إضمار أن، المعنى لأن يفسد فيها، وعطف ويهلك

ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r2.speaker: قالوا
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r2.claim: One reported interpretation takes al-ḥarth and al-nasl as women and children; this is plausible because a woman is called ḥarth, by comparison with what is cultivated and bears produce.
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r2.anchor: وقالوا في (الحرث والنسل): إن الحرث النساء والنسل الأولاد.

ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r3.speaker: قالوا
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r3.claim: Another interpretation keeps al-ḥarth as crops: corruption and disorder in the land ruin agriculture.
ZAJJAJ:v1p277/r3.anchor: وقالوا في الحرث هو ما تعرفه من الزرع. لأنه إذا أفسد في الأرض أبطل

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r1.claim: Most commentators infer conscious intent; Asad says li may instead mark consequence regardless of intent, and his rendering leaves both readings open.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r1.anchor: the particle li in li-yufsida (generally taken to mean "in order that he might spread corruption") plays in this context

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r2.claim: Harth primarily means gain or acquisition through labour, and can denote worldly goods, crops, or the cultivated land itself; 'tilth' can metaphorically mean human and social endeavours.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r2.anchor: its primary significance is "gain" or "acquisition" through labour; and thus it often signifies "worldly goods"

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r3.speaker: some commentators
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r3.claim: Some commentators, citing 2:223, take harth here to mean wives, so destroying tilth and progeny means disrupting family life and the social fabric.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r3.anchor: some commentators - basing their opinion on the Qur'anic sentence, "your wives are your tilth" (2:223)- maintain that harth stands here for "wives"

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r4.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r4.claim: On either reading, making this worldly-only attitude the basis of social behavior inevitably causes widespread moral decay and social disintegration.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n189/r4.anchor: and made the basis of social behaviour, it unavoidably results in widespread moral decay

IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r3.claim: When the man leaves the Prophet, he spreads corruption through the land and destroys crops and offspring.
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : قال تعالى: وإذا تولى 2: 205: أي خرج من عندك سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها

IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r4.claim: God's not loving corruption means that He does not love or approve the man's conduct.
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r4.anchor: ويهلك الحرث والنسل، والله لا يحب الفساد 2: 205 أي لا يحب عمله ولا يرضاه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says “cultivation” means crops and “offspring” means the offspring of every kind of thing.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ويهلك الحرث والنسل ﴾ قال الحرث الحرث والنسل نسل كل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r8.claim: Nasl is a verbal noun for emerging quickly, as wool, hair, or feathers come loose and fall from an animal or bird.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r8.anchor: النسل: مصدر: نسل ينسل، وأصله الخروج بسرعة ومن قولهم: نسل وبر البعير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r9.claim: Another account takes nasl as successive emergence, illustrated by the repeated falling of a bird’s feathers and a poem about clothes coming away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r9.anchor: وقيل: النسل الخروج متتابعا، ومنه: نسال الطائر ما تتابع سقوطه من ريشه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r10.claim: Calling offspring nasl transfers a verbal noun to its object: offspring emerge from the father’s back and quickly issue from the mother’s womb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r10.anchor: والإطلاق على الولد نسلا من إطلاق المصدر على المفعول، يسمى بذلك لخروجه من ظهر الأب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.claim: Al-Suddi's version says al-Akhnas passed Muslim crops and donkeys, burned the crops, and spared the donkeys.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: فمر بزرع للمسلمين وحمر، فأحرق الزرع، وغفر الحمر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r10.claim: The basic sense of تولى is to turn away physically, extended here to turning away from a prior word or deed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r10.anchor: حقيقة التولي الانصراف بالبدن، ثم اتسع فيه حتى استعمل فيما يرجع عنه من قول وفعل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says تولى means he became angry, turning away from his earlier agreeable manner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: غضب لأنه رجوع عن الرضى الذي كان قبله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r12.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says he turned away from the statement he had made.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: انصرف عن القول الذي قاله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r13.speaker: مقاتل وابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r13.claim: Muqatil and Ibn Qutayba take تولى literally as departing with one's body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل، وابن قتيبة: انصرف ببدنه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r14.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r14.claim: Mujahid derives تولى from ولاية: the man becomes a governor or authority.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من الولاية، أي: صار واليا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r15.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r15.claim: They take سعى literally as moving quickly on foot; Ibn Abbas's attribution is cited through Ibn Atiyya, and the scene is his departure from Muhammad followed by road-cutting and corruption like al-Akhnas against Thaqif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r15.anchor: والسعي حقيقة المشي بالقدمين بسرعة، وعلى ذلك حمله هنا أبو سليمان الدمشقي، وابن عباس، فيما ذكر ابن عطية عنه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r1.claim: سعى can mean action or striving in Arabic, as shown by the Qur'anic statements in 53:39 and 17:19.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r1.anchor: وقيل: السعي هنا العمل، وهو مجاز سائغ في استعمال العرب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r2.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses أسعى for pursuing a livelihood or an enduring glory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r2.anchor: وقال الشاعر: فلو أن ما أسعى لأدنى معيشة ... كفاني، ولم أطلب، قليل من المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r3.speaker: الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r3.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line uses سعى for active effort on behalf of Kinda, helping them drive off an enemy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r3.anchor: وقال الأعشى: وسعى لكندة غير سعي مواكل ... قيس فصد عدوها ونبالها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r4.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r4.claim: Another poet uses أسعى for working on behalf of the Banu Malik clan; the line says each person strives at his own task.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r4.anchor: وقال آخر: أسعى على حيي بني مالك ... كل امرئ في شأنه ساع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r5.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r5.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj, and a report from Ibn Abbas take the phrase as scheming against Islam; some specify disbelief, others injustice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r5.anchor: والمعنى: سعى بحيله وإدارة الدوائر على الإسلام، وإلى هذا القول نحا مجاهد، وابن جريج، وذكر أيضا عن ابن عباس:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r6.claim: Saʿy can also be done by speech: carrying a tale between people to provoke division, as the cited anonymous verse illustrates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r6.anchor: وقد يقع السعي بالقول، يقال: سعى بين فلان وفلان نقل إليهما قولا يوجب الفرقة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r7.claim: Although striving already occurs on earth, في الأرض generalizes the place wherever he settles and suggests extensive, repeated movement through the earth; compare 2:11.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r7.anchor: في الأرض، معلوم أن السعي لا يكون إلا في الأرض، لكن أفاد العموم بمعنى في: أي مكان حل منها سعى للفساد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r8.claim: If the referent is al-Akhnas, الأرض means Medina by prior reference.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r8.anchor: وإذا كان المراد الأخنس فالأرض أرض المدينة، فالألف واللام للعهد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r9.claim: The لام clause gives the purpose and motive of his striving.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r9.anchor: ليفسد فيها، هذا علة سعيه، والحامل له على السعي في الأرض،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r10.claim: Corruption is the opposite of right order and defiance of God's command in 11:61; it includes injustice, killing, plunder, captivity, and disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r10.anchor: والفساد يكون بأنواع من: الجور، والقتل، والنهب، والسبي، ويكون: بالكفر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r11.claim: The destruction of crops and offspring is a further motive, although included under corruption; they are singled out as the greatest harm to worldly settlement, in a general-then-particular construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r11.anchor: ولكنه خصهما بالذكر لأنهما أعظم ما يحتاج إليه في عمارة الدنيا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r12.claim: Those who explain فساد as destruction take the crops-and-offspring phrase as detail after the general statement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p328/r12.anchor: من فسر الإفساد بالتخريب، جعل هذا من باب التفصيل بعد الإجمال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r1.claim: On the al-Akhnas account, الحرث means crops and النسل means breeding animals, specifically the donkeys he killed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r1.anchor: وعلى ما تقدم من أن الآية في الأخنس، يكون الحرث الزرع، والنسل الحمر التي قتلها، فيكون النسل المراد به الدواب ذوات النسل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r2.speaker: الزجاج وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj, as reported by Ibn Atiyya, offers women as الحرث and children as النسل; this is a euphemism and a figure of bayan, linked to 2:223.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r2.anchor: وذكره ابن عطية عن الزجاج احتمالا، فيكون من الكناية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r3.claim: The majority read ويهلك from أهلك, coordinating it with ليفسد, with crops and offspring as objects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ويهلك، من أهلك. عطفا على: ليفسد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r4.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r4.claim: Ubayy reads وليهلك, making the purpose-لام explicit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبي: وليهلك، بإظهار لام العلة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r5.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r5.claim: Some read from أهلك with the verb raised; it may coordinate with يعجبك or سعى understood as يسعى, or begin a new sentence with an omitted هو.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r5.anchor: وقرأ قوم: ويهلك، من أهلك، وبرفع الكاف. وخرج على أن يكون عطفا على قوله: يعجبك، أو على: سعى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r6.speaker: الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r6.claim: These readers use هلك with a raised verb and make crops and offspring its subjects; related transmissions are reported from Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وابن أبي إسحاق، وأبو حيوة، وابن محيصن: ويهلك من هلك، وبرفع الكاف، والحرث والنسل على الفاعلية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r7.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r7.claim: Al-Mahdawi says Hamad's report from Ibn Kathir was actually from أهلك with the verb raised and crops accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r7.anchor: وحكى المهدوي أن الذي رواه حماد عن ابن كثير، إنما هو: ويهلك من أهلك، وبضم الكاف، الحرث بالنصب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r8.speaker: قوم والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r8.claim: Another group reads هلك with fatha on the lām, a raised verb, and crops as subject; Zamakhshari attributes it to Hasan and calls the dialect irregular, like ركن يركن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r8.anchor: وقرأ قوم: ويهلك من هلك، وبفتح اللام، ورفع الكاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r9.claim: Zamakhshari reports a passive reading from Hasan and counts six readings: the first three leave the crops accusative, while the latter three raise them as subjects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وروي عنه، يعني عن الحسن، ويهلك مبنيا للمفعول، فيكون في هذه اللفظة ست قراءات:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r10.claim: The conditional sentence beginning وإذا تولى may stand independently after a pause at ألد الخصام, or be coordinated with the relative clause or description of من.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r10.anchor: وهذه الجملة الشرطية إما مستأنفة، وتم الكلام عند قوله: وهو ألد الخصام، وإما معطوفة على صلة من أو صفتها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r11.claim: The verse states that God does not love corruption; the destruction of crops and offspring is already covered by the broader corruption.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r11.anchor: فأخبر تعالى أنه لا يحب الفساد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r12.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r12.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that God does not will corruption: what occurs is not willed or done by Him, since an agent cannot perform what He does not will; they equate love with will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r12.anchor: وقد تعلقت المعتزلة بهذه الآية في أن الله لا يريد الفساد، فما وقع منه فليس مراد الله تعالى، ولا مفعولا له،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan signals a contradiction in the Muʿtazili argument that God's love must equal His will and that He cannot love something while not willing it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p330/r13.anchor: وفي هذا ما فيه من التناقض. انتهى ما قالوا:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r1.claim: Reported interpretations specify corruption in religion, supply أهل before الفساد, gloss it as sins God does not approve (Ibn Abbas), or use love figuratively for command: God does not command corruption.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r1.anchor: وقيل: المعنى والله لا يحب الفساد دينا، وقيل: هو على حذف مضاف أي: أهل الفساد، وقال ابن عباس: المعنى لا يرضى المعاصي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r2.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r2.claim: Al-Raghib defines corruption as moving something from a praiseworthy state without a valid purpose, which does not occur in God's acts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r2.anchor: وقال الراغب: الإفساد إخراج الشيء من حالة محمودة لا لغرض صحيح، وذلك غير موجود في فعل الله تعالى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r3.claim: These interpretive maneuvers generally follow theologians who take divine love to mean will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r3.anchor: وهذه التأويلات كلها هو على ما ذهب إليه المتكلمون من أن الحب بمعنى الإرادة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says love adds a quality of preference beyond will; because God loves only what is wholly good, corruption can be willed without being loved.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والحب له على الإرادة مزية إيثار، فلو قال أحد: إن الفساد المراد تنقصه مزية الإيثار لصح ذلك إذ الحب من الله تعالى إنما هو لما حسن من جميع جهاته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r5.speaker: جمهور العلماء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r5.claim: The majority reject the Muʿtazili equation of love and will: a person may want a painful wound without loving it, and 39:7 likewise says God does not approve disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r5.anchor: وجمهور العلماء على خلاف ذلك، والفرق بين الإرادة والمحبة بين، فإن الإنسان يريد بطيء الجرح ولا يحبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r6.claim: For God, love and its absence are contradictories with no intermediate state; for other beings they are contraries, leaving an intermediate state possible.
