ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r6.anchor: وجاء في كتاب الله تعالى نفي محبة الله تعالى أشياء، إذ لا واسطة بين الحب وعدمه بالنسبة إليه تعالى، بخلاف غيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r7.claim: In its apparent general sense, corruption covers every kind in land, property, or religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r7.anchor: وظاهر الفساد يعم كل فساد في أرض أو مال أو دين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r8.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r8.claim: Ata infers from God's dislike of corruption a prohibition on tearing one's garment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r8.anchor: وقد استدل عطاء بقوله: والله لا يحب الفساد على منع شق الإنسان ثوبه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says corruption here means ruin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الفساد هنا الخراب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r3.claim: When he leaves, he moves through the land for corruption and destruction of crops and offspring, the foundations of existence; God therefore does not love what he does.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى سبب سعيه وأنه للإفساد مطلقا، وليهلك الحرث والنسل اللذين هما قوام الوجود

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r1.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets تولى as turning away and withdrawing.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r1.anchor: أي أدبر وأعرض قاله الحسن أو إذا غلب وصار واليا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets تولى as gaining power and becoming a governor.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r2.anchor: قاله الضحاك أن ( الحرث ) هنا النساء ( والنسل ) الأولاد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r3.claim: One reported interpretation takes الحرث as women and النسل as children.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r3.anchor: أن ( الحرث ) هنا النساء ( والنسل ) الأولاد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r4.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq interprets الحرث as religion and النسل as people.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r4.anchor: وعن الصادق أن الحرث في هذا الموضع الدين والنسل الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r5.claim: A reading makes the verb intransitive, with الحرث والنسل nominative and coordinated with سعى.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r5.anchor: على أن الفعل للحرث والنسل والرفع للعطف

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan is reported to read the verb with fatḥa on lām, a dialectal form, and also with passive voice.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بفتح اللام وهي لغة أبى يأبى وروى عنه ويهلك على البناء للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r7.claim: God does not approve of corruption; the parenthetical statement warns of punishment, and mentioning فساد suffices because the general term includes the specific harms just described.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r7.anchor: لايرضى به فأحذروا غضبه عليه والجملة إعتراض للوعيد وأكتفى فيها على الفساد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r8.claim: Corruption is taking something from a praiseworthy state without a sound purpose, which is not found in God’s acts or commands; apparent corruption is relative to us, while all divine action is good.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r8.anchor: لأنه يقال : الإفسادكما قيل في الحقيقة إخراج الشيء عن حالة محمودة لا لغرض صحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r9.claim: God’s destruction of animals for food serves humanity, the world’s central purpose; death also enables everlasting life and return to the original homeland.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p95/r9.anchor: وأما أمره بإهلاك الحيوان مثلا لأكله فلإصلاح الإنسان الذي هو زبدة هذا العالم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r2.claim: Tawallā means that he turns away or withdraws.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r2.anchor: {وإذا تولى} أي أدبر وأعرض عنك {سعى في الأرض}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r3.claim: Saʿā can mean that he worked in the land; another gloss is that he traveled or walked through it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r3.anchor: {سعى في الأرض} أي عمل فيها، وقيل: سار فيها ومشى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the corruption as severing kinship ties and spilling Muslim blood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج قطع الرحم وسفك دماء المسلمين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r5.claim: The author says al-Akhnas had a dispute with Thaqif and attacked them at night, burning their crops and destroying their livestock.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r5.anchor: فبيتهم ليلة فأحرق زروعهم وأهلك مواشيهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r6.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r6.claim: Muqatil says al-Akhnas went to Taif to collect a debt, burned the debtor's grain stack, and hamstrung his donkey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: خرج إلى الطائف مقتضيا مالا له على غريم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r7.claim: Nasl means the offspring of every animal, including human beings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r7.anchor: والنسل: نسل كل دابة والناس منهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r8.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak reads tawallā as taking charge and becoming a governor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {وإذا تولى} أي ملك الأمر وصار واليا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r9.claim: Mujahid says that when he gained authority and acted unjustly, God withheld rain and destroyed crops and offspring.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد: في قوله عز وجل {وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض} قال إذا ولي فعمل بالعدوان والظلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r10.claim: God does not approve of corruption.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r10.anchor: {والله لا يحب الفساد} أي لا يرضى بالفساد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says cutting a dirham short is corruption in the land.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r11.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: قطع الدرهم من الفساد في الأرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r1.claim: Tawallā means that he turned away and departed from you, or that he prevailed and became a governor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r1.anchor: أدبر وانصرف عنك. وقيل: إذا غلب وصار واليا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r2.claim: One explanation compares the destruction to al-Akhnaṣ’s attack on Thaqīf: he raided them at night, burned crops, and killed livestock.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r2.anchor: كما فعله الأخنس بثقيف إذ بيتهم وأحرق زروعهم وأهلك مواشيهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r3.claim: Another explanation applies the phrase to evil rulers who kill and destroy property.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r3.anchor: أو كما يفعله ولاة السوء بالقتل والإتلاف

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r4.claim: A further explanation says oppression may lead God, because of its ill omen, to withhold rain, destroying crops and offspring.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r4.anchor: أو بالظلم حتى يمنع الله بشؤمه القطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:205/r5.claim: God does not approve of corruption, so beware His wrath against the corrupt person.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r1.claim: The next verse explains how the hypocrite's contentiousness appears in action.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر أنه ألد شرع يذكر وجه لدده فقال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r2.claim: Tawalla can mean turning away inwardly or leaving the person he had deceived with his speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r2.anchor: أي أعرض بقلبه أو قاله عمن خدعه بكلامه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r3.claim: The verb saʿā depicts him hastening with full effort to stir discord.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r3.anchor: وكنى بالتعبير بالسعي عن الإسراع في إيقاع الفتنة بغاية الجهد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r4.claim: Fasād is a name for all sins; his actions and words spread corruption throughout the land, especially among supporters.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r4.anchor: أي كلها بفعله وقوله عند من يوافقه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r5.claim: His initial aim is to corrupt relations and enlist accomplices to bring destruction; destruction then enables further corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r5.anchor: ونظمت الآية هكذا إفهاما لأن المعنى أن غرضه أولا بإفساد ذات البين التوصل إلى الإهلاك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r6.claim: Al-harth means cultivated produce on which animals live; al-Harali says it is named for human cultivation, unlike planting attributed to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r6.anchor: أي المحروث الذي يعيش به الحيوان , قال الحرالي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r7.claim: Harvest is a cause of animal life: destroying the cause destroys its effect, while the reverse is not necessarily true.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r7.anchor: ولأنه إذا هلك السبب هلك المسبب من غير عكس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r8.claim: Al-nasl means offspring, through which the animal kind continues.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r8.anchor: أي المنسول الذي به بقاء نوع الحيوان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r9.claim: Al-Harali defines nasl as the subtle part extracted from a whole.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r9.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو استخراج لطيف الشيء من جملته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r10.claim: God neither commands nor approves corruption; He forbids it, changes it, and punishes it even when punishment is delayed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r10.anchor: لا يفعل فيه فعل المحب فلا يأمر به بل ينهى عنه ولا يقر عليه بل يغيره وإن طال المدى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r11.claim: The verse says corruption rather than destruction because destruction may be outward only and beneficial, as in requital.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r11.anchor: لأنه قد يكون صورة فقط فيكون صلاحا كما إذا كان قصاصا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r12.claim: Fasād is chosen over ifsād because the latter can include corruption caused without intent.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r12.anchor: ولا قال : الإفساد يشمل ما إذا كان الفساد عن غير قصد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r13.claim: The passage uses ihtibāk: corruption mentioned first implies its omission later, while destruction mentioned second implies its omission first.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r13.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك , ذكر أولا الإفساد ليدل على حذفه ثانيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r14.claim: A second ihtibāk pairs harvest as cause, implying offspring, and offspring as effect, implying crops.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r14.anchor: وذكر الحرث الذي هو السبب دلالة على الناسل والنسل الذي هو المسبب دلالة على الزرع

DURR-FULL:v1p571/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r4.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbas’s account, when the man leaves, he acts to corrupt the land and destroy crops and offspring; God neither loves nor approves his work.
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r4.anchor: خرج من عندك (سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها

DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.claim: The continuing report says the verse concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who professed sincere Islam to the Prophet in Medina, impressed him, then burned a Muslim’s crops and hamstrung his donkeys after leaving.
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.anchor: قال نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي حليف لبني زهرة أقبل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses the man’s striving as working in the land, the tilth as its plants, and offspring as the young of all animals, humans and beasts.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد {وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض} قال: عمل في الأرض {ويهلك الحرث}

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r4.claim: Mujahid says unjust rule and oppression lead God to withhold rain, destroying crops and offspring; he links this to 30:41, where corruption on land and sea comes from human deeds.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r4.anchor:
عن مجاهد
أنه سئل عن قوله {وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض} قال:

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the tilth as crops and offspring as the young of every animal.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن قوله {ويهلك الحرث والنسل} قال: الحرث الزرع

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas adds that the offspring of every animal includes people as well.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: النسل نسل كل دابة الناس أيضا

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses offspring as birds and beasts and cites a line of poetry using nasl for descendants as Arabic evidence.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r7.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله {الحرث والنسل}

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r8.claim: ʿIkrima says a pilgrim lacking sandals may wear leather socks and, when asked whether to slit them, invokes God’s dislike of corruption as reason not to cut them.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: يتخفف المحرم إذا لم يجد نعلين

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says turning away means leaving the Prophet's presence; al-Suddī is reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : واذا تولى اي : خرج من عندك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r2.claim: Mujāhid takes it as ruling the land and acting with aggression and injustice.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قال : قيل يا أبا الحجاج : كيف توليه فيها ؟ قال : يلي في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses striving in the land as working in it.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ، قوله : سعى عمل في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r4.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ glosses the crop as cultivated plants, which are cut down and spoiled.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r4.anchor: قال : قلت العطاء : واذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها قال الحرث : الزرع ، يقطعه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r5.claim: Qatāda says he corrupts the land and devastates God's servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r5.anchor: عن قتادة : ليفسد فيها قال : يفسد في ارض ، مهلك لعباد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r6.claim: Mālik regards corruption in the land as comparable to killing.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r6.anchor: قال لي مالك : قال الله عز وجل : واذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها فراى مالك ، ان الفساد في الأرض ، مثل القتل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says destroying crops means burning what people cultivate.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r7.anchor: عن ابي العالية : ويهلك الحرث قال : يحرق الحرث الذي يحرثه الناس ، نبات الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r8.claim: Al-Suddī is reported to give the same explanation.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ḥarth as cultivation or crops.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r9.anchor: عن التميمي ، قال : سالت ابن عباس

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r10.speaker: أبو العالية ومجاهد وعطاء وعكرمة والربيع بن أنس وقتادة ومكحول والسدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r10.claim: These authorities are reported to gloss ḥarth as crops.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r10.anchor: وروى عن أبي العالية ومجاهد وعطاء وعكرمة والربيع بن انس وقتادة ومكحول والسدى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r11.claim: Mujāhid says oppression withholds rain, whose absence destroys crops and offspring.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p366/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قيل له : يا أبا الحجاج

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses ḥarth as al-ḥannān and the established root.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r1.anchor: عن لضحاك في قوله : ويهلك الحرث قل : اما الحرث ، فهو الحنان ، والاصل الثابت

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says offspring means the offspring of every animal.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r2.anchor: عن أبي اسحاق عن التميمي ، قالت سالت ابن عباس ، عن قول الله : ويهلك الحرث والنسل قال : نسل كل دابة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r3.speaker: عكرمة وأبو العالية ومكحول والربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r3.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r3.anchor: وروى عن عكرمة , أبي العالية ومكحول والربيع بن انس ، نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also includes human offspring along with every animal.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r4.anchor: عن عبد لله بن عباس ، قوله : ويهلك الحرث والنسل فنسل كل دابة والناس ايضا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r5.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r5.claim: Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, and Qatāda are reported to include humans as well.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r5.anchor: وروى عن مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God neither loves nor approves corruption.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس : والله لا يحب الفساد اي : لا يجب عمله ولا يرضى به

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib counts cutting silver and gold as corruption in the land.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r7.anchor: انه سمع سعيد بن المسيب يقول : قطع الورق والذهب من الفساد في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r8.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r8.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is reported to give the same view.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p367/r8.anchor: وروى عن عمر بن عبد العزيز ، نحو ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r7.claim: Other verses establish reform of the world as an aim of the Lawgiver, including 47:22–23 and this warning against destroying crops and offspring.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r7.anchor: وقد دلت آيات كثيرة على أن إصلاح العالم مقصد للشارع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r1.claim: Idhā here is a temporal adverb containing conditional force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض } إذا ظرف تضمن معنى الشرط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r2.claim: One derivation takes tawallā as turning away or departing, with an omitted “from you” addressed to the Prophet; this recalls 2:142's question about what turned them from the qibla.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r2.anchor: و { تولى } إما مشتق من التولية وهي الإدبار والانصراف يقال ولى وتولى وقد تقدم قوله تعالى : { ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم } ( البقرة : 142 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r3.claim: Alternatively, tawallā derives from assuming authority: when the person becomes leader, he works corruption; Ibn Ashur relates this to al-Akhnas's leadership of his allies, Banu Zuhra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r3.anchor: وإما مشتق من الولاية : يقال ولي البلد وتولاه ، أي وإذا صار واليا أي إذا تزعم ورأس الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r4.claim: Saʿā literally means to walk briskly, as in the man who came running from the far side of the city at 28:20.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r4.anchor: وقوله : { سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها } السعي حقيقته المشي الحثيث قال تعالى : { وجاء رجل من أقصا المدينة يسعى } ( القصص : 20 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r5.claim: Saʿy also means work and earning, as in the statement about striving for the Hereafter at 17:19.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r5.anchor: ويطلق السعي على العمل والكسب ، قال تعالى : { ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها } ( الإسراء : 19 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r6.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r6.claim: Ibn Kulthum's line uses sāʿī for a person who mediates among people to reconcile disputes; Labid's verse is also cited in support of this sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r6.anchor: قال عمرو بن كلثوم : ومنا قبله الساعي كليب فأي الفضل إلا قد ولينا وقال لبيد : وهم السعاة إذا العشيرة أفظعت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r7.claim: Saʿy can also mean exerting effort and resolve to accomplish something, as in Pharaoh's conduct at 79:22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r7.anchor: ويطلق على الحرص وبذل العزم لتحصيل شيء كما قال تعالى في شأن فرعون { ثم أدبر يسعى } ( النازعات : 22 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r8.claim: Here the word can carry its literal sense and the sense of deliberate striving: he goes about as a raider, corrupting the land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r8.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون هنا بالمعنيين الأول والرابع أي ذهب يسير في الأرض غازيا ومغيرا ليفسد فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r9.claim: The verse may allude to al-Akhnas's destruction of crops belonging to some Muslims, exposing the falseness of his professed affection for the Prophet and his followers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r9.anchor: فيكون إشارة إلى ما فعله الأخنس بزرع بعض المسلمين ، لأن ذلك مؤذن بكفره وكذبه في مودة النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r10.claim: Some exegetes instead say al-Akhnas attacked Thaqif, burning their crops and killing their livestock, despite their being his own people and non-Muslims at the time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r10.anchor: أو إلى ما صنعه بزرع ثقيف على قول من قال من المفسرين إن الأخنس بيت ثقيفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r11.claim: Because the attack was neither to aid Islam nor to bring people to faith, and brought no benefit, it revealed a corrupt disposition at odds with his kind public speech; God disapproves needless harm even to unbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p268/r11.anchor: لم يفعله انتصارا للإسلام ولم يكن في حالة حرب معهم فكان فعله ينم عن خبث طوية لا تتطابق مع ما يظهره من الخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r1.claim: He first reads سعى literally as movement through the land for corruption—raiding and theft not undertaken to exalt God’s word—and takes ليفسد as its purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r1.anchor: وقوله : { في الأرض } تأكيد لمدلول { سعى } لرفع توهم المجاز من أن يراد بالسعي العمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r2.claim: Alternatively, سعى can mean intending and devising corruption; ليفسد is then its object, with a communicative lam and implicit أن, as in 2:185 and 9:32.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { سعى } مجازا في الإرادة والتدبير أي دبر الكيد لأن ابتكار الفساد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r3.claim: The line attributed to Juʾz ibn Kulaib al-Faqʿasi illustrates wanting expressed with a lam; al-Marzūqī reads تبغى ليستاد as seeking to capture, with the infinitive as object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r3.anchor: وقول جزء بنن كليبب الفقعسي : تبغى ابن كوز والسفاهة كاسمها ليستاد منا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r4.claim: An eloquent speaker may use a causal lam where its action is both the cause and object; the object reading is recoverable by construing an implicit أن.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r4.anchor: وأقول : إن هذا الاستعمال يتأتى في كل موضع يقع فيه مفعول الفعل علة للفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r5.claim: في الأرض attaches to سعى and specifies activity among the people of their land; the repeated فيها explicates the first phrase and reinforces it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269/r5.anchor: ويكون قوله : { في الأرض } متعلقا بسعى لإفادة أن سعيه في أمر من أمور أهل أرضكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r1.claim: With the yāʾ read with ḍamma, the verb means that he destroys the crops and offspring.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { ويهلك الحرث والنسل } بضم الياء أي يتلفه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r2.claim: Here الحرث means crops, while النسل means animal young and derives from wool falling away and separating.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r2.anchor: والحرث هنا مراد منه الزرع ، والنسل أطفال الحيوان مشتق من نسل الصوف نسولا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r3.claim: He prefers taking crops and offspring as a proverbial image for destroying what sustains people, who relied on cultivation and livestock, rather than as only those two things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r3.anchor: وعندي أن إهلاك الحرث والنسل كناية عن اختلال ما به قوام أحوال الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r4.claim: An alternative says crops and offspring allude specifically to what al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq did.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r4.anchor: وقيل الحرث والنسل هنا إشارة إلى ما صنع الأخنس بن شريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r5.claim: Whichever reading is chosen, the verse makes such a perpetrator liable to punishment in the afterlife; the closing clause warns and rebukes him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r5.anchor: فالآية دالة على أن من ينتسب في مثل ذلك صريحا أو كناية مستحق للعقاب في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r6.claim: Negating divine love means negating approval, since love as an affective inclination toward appreciation cannot apply to God; he says approval means will for his school and the Muʿtazilites, an issue tied to the creation of acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى نفي المحبة نفي الرضا بالفساد ، وإلا فالمحبة وهي انفعال النفس وتوجه طبيعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r7.claim: An all-powerful God who disapproves of an act can punish its perpetrator, because no obstacle can prevent Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r7.anchor: ولا شك أن القدير إذا لم يرض بشيء يعاقب فاعله ، إذ لا يعوقه عن ذلك عائق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r8.claim: Destroying crops is called corruption even if they belong to polytheists, because losing the earth’s goods harms everyone; fighting may destroy only things that enable destruction and aggression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r8.anchor: وإن كان الزرع والحرث للمشركين : لأن إتلاف خيرات الأرض رزء على الناس كلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r9.claim: Corruption destroys benefits that are wholly or predominantly useful: milk is wholly useful, and firewood predominantly so; destroying marginal benefits such as wine, or things with no benefit such as pests, is not corruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r9.anchor: والفساد ضد الصلاح ، ومعنى الفساد : إتلاف ما هو نافع للناس نفعا محضا أو راجحا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r10.claim: Corruption disables the wise purposes for which God created things for people. War destroys a predominant harm, so burning homes or cutting trees is prohibited unless retaining them would strengthen the enemy, prolong fighting, and risk Muslim defeat; necessity is limited to its measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p269#2/r10.anchor: ومن أجل ذلك نهي عن إحراق الديار في الحرب وعن قطع الأشجار إلا إذا رجح في نظر أمير الجيش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.claim: The passage teaches believers to discern inner realities and not be deceived by appearances before testing: a person may speak sweetly and look good while concealing evil and plotting harm.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and other scholars generalize the passage to anyone concealing unbelief, hypocrisy, lies, or harm while speaking otherwise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء: نزلت هذه الآيات في كل مبطن كفر أو نفاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.speaker: الترمذي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.claim: A report cited in al-Tirmidhi from a divine book describes people with honey-sweet tongues and bitter hearts, who use religion for worldly gain and face a confounding trial.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.anchor: وهي تشبه ما ورد في الترمذي أن في بعض كتب الله تعالى: «أن من عباد الله قوما ألسنتهم أحلى من العسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r3.speaker: ابن جريج وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r3.claim: On the inward-action reading, tawallā means he turned aside, grew angry and proud, then schemed to bring calamity on Islam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r3.anchor: ونحا هذا المنحى في معنى الآية ابن جريج وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r4.claim: The inward striving is likened to the striving in 53:39 and 17:19.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r4.anchor: ومن هذا السعي قول الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r5.claim: A poetic line about striving for Banu Malik illustrates saʿā as purposeful effort.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r5.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: [الرجز] أسعى على حي بني مالك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r6.claim: On the physical-action reading, he turns away from Muhammad, gets up, walks across the land, and corrupts it; both readings describe corruption.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r6.anchor: نحا هذا المنحى ابن عباس وغيره، وكلا السعيين فساد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r7.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r7.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the reference as al-Akhnas burning crops and killing donkeys.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r7.anchor: قال الطبري: «المراد الأخنس في إحراقه الزرع وقتله الحمر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r8.claim: Mujahid says a wrongdoer’s corruption leads God to withhold rain, destroying crops and offspring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «المراد أن الظالم يفسد في الأرض فيمسك الله المطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r9.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r9.claim: Another interpretation says the corruptor kills people, ending cultivation and the generations who tend it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r9.anchor: وقيل: المراد أن المفسد يقتل الناس فينقطع عمار الزرع والمنسلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows al-harth to mean women and al-nasl their offspring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «يحتمل أن يراد بالحرث النساء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r11.claim: The apparent sense is an emphatic image of corruption: worldly affairs chiefly turn on cultivation and procreation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r11.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: والظاهر أن الآية عبارة عن مبالغة في الإفساد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r12.speaker: أكثر القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r12.claim: Most readers use yuhliku, coordinated with yufsidu; Ubayy’s codex adds a conjunction before it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r12.anchor: وأكثر القراء على يهلك بضم الياء وكسر اللام وفتح الكاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r13.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r13.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s codex reads wa-li-yuhlik.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r14.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r14.claim: Some read yahliku with a ḍamma on kāf, coordinating it with yaʿjibuka, with saʿā as a future verb, or as a new sentence.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r15.speaker: الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r15.claim: These readers use yahlaku with nominative al-harth and al-nasl; the same reading is transmitted from Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r15.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن «ويهلك» بفتح الياء وكسر اللام وضم الكاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r16.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r16.claim: Al-Mahdawi says Hammad ibn Salama’s transmission from Ibn Kathir has yuhliku with al-harth accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r16.anchor: وحكى المهدوي أن الذي روى حماد بن سلمة عن ابن كثير إنما هو «ويهلك» بضم الياء والكاف «الحرث» بالنصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r17.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r17.claim: Some read yahlak with fatḥa on yāʾ and lām and nominative al-harth, using the dialect halaka yahlak, classed as anomalous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r17.anchor: وقرأ قوم «ويهلك» بفتح الياء واللام ورفع «الحرث» وهي لغة هلك يهلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r18.claim: Al-harth literally means plowing soil; by association it also means crops and extends to trees and orchards.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r18.anchor: والحرث في اللغة شق الأرض للزراعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r19.claim: In 21:78, al-harth is understood in the commentaries as a vineyard.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r19.anchor: ومنه قول عز وجل إذ يحكمان في الحرث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r20.claim: Women are called cultivation by way of metaphor.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r21.claim: Nasl derives from nasala, to emerge in succession; it also describes a bird’s successive loss of feathers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r21.anchor: والنسل مأخوذ من نسل ينسل إذا خرج متتابعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r22.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r22.claim: The same root appears in 21:96, describing people streaming down from every rise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r22.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى: وهم من كل حدب ينسلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r23.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r23.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s line using tansilu illustrates the root’s sense of successive emergence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r23.anchor: ومنه قول امرئ القيس: [الطويل] فسلي ثيابي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r24.speaker: المتكلمون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r24.claim: On the theologians’ account that love means will, God does not approve corruption religiously, though corruption does occur by His will.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r24.anchor: ولا يحب معناه لا يحبه من أهل الصلاح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.claim: The preceding verses appear to concern unbelievers generally; sinners sharing these traits also incur a portion of the warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.anchor: والظاهر من هذا التقسيم أن تكون الآيات قبل هذا على العموم في الكافر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r12.claim: Love has an added element of preference over will; corruption may be willed without such preference, since God loves only what is wholly good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r12.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: والحب له على الإرادة مزية إيثار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.claim: The report says this verse and the next three were revealed concerning al-Zubayr, al-Miqdad, Khubayb and the other expedition members, as well as the hypocrites.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في الزبير والمقداد وخبيب وأصحابه والمنافقين هذه الآية وثلاث آيات بعدها وهذا الحديث بطوله مروي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj take tawalla to mean that the person became angry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r1.anchor: فيه اربعة أقوال أحدها أنه بمعنى غضب روي عن ابن عباس وابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan takes tawalla to mean turning away from the speech he had made.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه الانصراف عن القول الذي قاله قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak take tawalla as holding authority or becoming a governor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r3.anchor: إذا صار واليا قاله مجاهد و الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r4.claim: Muqatil and Ibn Qutayba take tawalla as physically turning away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r4.anchor: والرابع أنه الانصراف بالبدن قاله مقاتل وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid take saʿa to mean acting or working.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r5.anchor: بمعنى عمل قاله ابن عباس و مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r6.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r6.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi takes saʿa literally as walking on foot.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r7.claim: The two reported meanings of fasad are unbelief and injustice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r7.anchor: وفي الفساد قولان أحدهما أنه الكفر والثاني الظلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وآخرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and others explain harth as crops and nasl as the offspring of every kind of animal.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r8.anchor: والحرث الزرع والنسل نسل كل شيء من الحيوان هذا قول ابن عباس وعكرمة في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج عن قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports a view that harth means women and nasl their children; he says this is reasonable because a woman is called harth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r9.anchor: وحكى الزجاج عن قوم أن الحرث النساء والنسل الأولاد قال وليس هذا بمنكر لأن المرأة تسمى حرثا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r10.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r10.claim: Most commentators say the destruction of crops and offspring is literal, by killing, burning, and other devastation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r10.anchor: أحدها أنه إهلاك ذلك بالقتل والإحراق والإفساد قاله الأكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r11.claim: Mujahid says oppression can stop rainfall and thereby destroy crops and offspring; this reading fits tawalla as becoming an authority.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r11.anchor: والثاني أنه إذا ظلم كان الظلم سببا لقطع القطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل قاله مجاهد وهو يخرج على قول من قال إنه من التولي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r12.claim: Some commentators say he destroys them through misguidance that ultimately leads to ruin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221#2/r12.anchor: والثالث أنه إهلاك ذلك بالضلال الذي يؤول إلى الهلاك حكاه بعض المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God does not approve of acts of disobedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس لا يرضى بالمعاصي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila use this verse to argue that God does not will corruption to exist.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r2.anchor: وقد احتجت المعتزلة بهذه الآية فأجاب أصحابنا بأجوبة منها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r3.claim: One response distinguishes God's religious or legal will from His will that things exist: He does not love corruption as religion, but that does not mean He did not will it to exist.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r3.anchor: منها أنه لا يحبه دينا ولا يريده شرعا فأما أنه لم يرده وجودا فلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r4.claim: A second response says God does not love corruption for believers, without extending that claim to unbelievers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه لا يحبه للمؤمنين دون الكافرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r5.claim: The relied-upon answer distinguishes will from love: a person may want bitter medicine or cauterization for a wound without loving either.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r5.anchor: والثالث أن الارادة معنى غير المحبة فإن الانسان قد يتناول المر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r6.claim: The author links this statement with God's saying that He does not approve disbelief for His servants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222/r6.anchor: وفي معنى هذه الآية قوله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.claim: The hypocrite's crooked speech is matched by evil action: his words are lies, belief corrupt, and deeds ugly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.anchor: هو أعوج المقال، سيئ الفعال، فذلك قوله، وهذا فعله: كلامه كذب، واعتقاده فاسد، وأفعاله قبيحة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r2.claim: Here saʿā means to intend or head toward something; the same sense occurs of Pharaoh in 79:22–26 and in the command to seek Friday prayer in 62:9.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r2.anchor: والسعي هاهنا هو: القصد. كما قال إخبارا عن فرعون: {ثم أدبر يسعى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r3.claim: The Prophetic sunnah forbids rushing physically to prayer and directs worshippers to arrive with calm and composure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r3.anchor: فإن السعي الحسي إلى الصلاة منهي عنه بالسنة النبوية: "إذا أتيتم الصلاة فلا تأتوها وأنتم تسعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r4.claim: The hypocrite's purpose is corruption and destruction of crops, where plants and fruit grow, and animal offspring; people depend on both for their livelihood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r4.anchor: ليس له همة إلا الفساد في الأرض، وإهلاك الحرث، وهو: محل نماء الزروع والثمار والنسل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r5.claim: Mujahid says that when people pursue corruption in the land, God withholds rain, so crops and livestock perish.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إذا سعى في الأرض فسادا، منع الله القطر، فهلك الحرث والنسل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r6.claim: God does not love anyone characterized by corruption or anyone who commits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r6.anchor: أي: لا يحب من هذه صفته، ولا من يصدر منه ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر والحسن
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and al-Hasan read yuhliku with nominative kāf as a new clause; the common reading makes it accusative, coordinated with the preceding verb.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والحسن: ويهلك برفع الكاف على الابتداء، وقراءة العامة بنصبها على العطف

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r9.claim: Nasl means offspring and derives from nasūl, going forth, because children succeed one another.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r9.anchor: والنسل: الولد، وأصله النسول، وهو الخروج، وسمي الأولاد نسلا لتناسل بعضهم بعد بعض

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r11.speaker: السدي والكلبي
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r11.claim: In that account, al-Akhnas later raided at night, killing livestock and burning crops.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r11.anchor: ثم بيت بني ثقيف، وأهلك مواشيهم، وأحرق زروعهم، وكان حسن العلانية سيئ السر

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r13.claim: At al-Rajiʿ seventy riders surrounded the Muslims, killed them, protected ʿAsim ibn Thabit's head from birds, and captured, killed, and crucified Khubayb; the verse came down about them.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r13.anchor: فركب سبعون راكبا، وأحاطوا بهم، وقتلوهم، وحمى الدبر رأس عاصم بن ثابت، وأسروا خبيبا، ثم قتلوه وصلبوه

JISHUMI:v1p835/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r10.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p835/r10.claim: Al-Hasan takes tawallā to mean that he turned away.

JISHUMI:v1p835/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v1p835/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says he turned away from the promise he had made.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r11.anchor: ولى عن قوله الذي أعطاه، عن ابن جريج

JISHUMI:v1p835/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r12.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v1p835/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets it as gaining control and becoming a ruler.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r12.anchor: ملك الأمر فصار واليا، عن الضحاك

JISHUMI:v1p835/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r13.claim: Saʿā fī al-arḍ can mean working in the land; al-Asamm says it means going away from Muhammad.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r13.anchor: أي عمل فيها، وقيل: سار من عندك عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v1p835/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r14.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v1p835/r14.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the corruption is severing kinship and spilling blood.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r14.anchor: ليقطع الرحم، ويسفك الدماء، عن ابن جريج

JISHUMI:v1p835/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r15.speaker: الأصم وغيره
JISHUMI:v1p835/r15.claim: Al-Asamm and others take it as displaying unbelief and committing sins.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r15.anchor: ليظهر الكفر ويعمل بالمعاصي، عن الأصم وغيره

JISHUMI:v1p835/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r16.claim: Al-ḥarth means crops, and al-nasl means offspring of every living creature.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r16.anchor: ويهلك الحرث النبات والنسل الأولاد المراد نسل كل حي

JISHUMI:v1p835/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r17.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p835/r17.claim: Al-Asamm says al-ḥarth means men and al-nasl means children.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r17.anchor: وقيل: الحرث: الرجال، والنسل، الأولاد، ذكره الأصم

JISHUMI:v1p835/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r18.claim: Here, God's not loving corruption means He does not will unbelief and disobedience.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r18.anchor: والله لا يحب لا يريد الفساد الكفر والمعاصي

JISHUMI:v1p835/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r23.claim: Because love applied to an act means willing it, the verse says God does not will sins, refuting the Mujbira doctrine of will.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r23.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يريد المعاصي؛ لأن المحبة متى علقت بالفعل، فالمراد الإرادة، فيبطل قول المجبرة في الإرادة

JISHUMI:v1p837/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p837/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p837/r1.claim: The verse refutes the claim that God creates corruption: if He created it, He would love it, yet it is impossible for Him to create something He does not love.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.claim: The phrase can mean when he turns away after sweetening his speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.anchor: عنك وذهب بعد إلانة القول وإحلاء المنطق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, when appointed to office, he behaves like wicked governors and spreads corruption.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.anchor: وإذا كان واليا فعل ما يفعل ولاة السوء من الفساد في الأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r8.claim: The corruption refers to what he did against Thaqif.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.claim: Another view says his injustice brings God’s withholding of rain, destroying crops and livestock.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.anchor: وقيل يظهر الظلم حتى يمنع الله بشؤم ظلمه القطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.claim: One reading makes crops and offspring the grammatical subjects, coordinated with “he strove”; al-Hasan reads the lām with fatḥa as dialect and also transmits a passive reading.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.anchor: وقرىء ( ويهلك الحرث والنسل ) على أن الفعل للحرث والنسل والرفع للعطف على سعى

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r17.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r17.claim: Al-Naqqash says tawalla means that the man became angry.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r18.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r18.claim: The apparent sense according to Hasan is that the man turned away.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r18.anchor: والثاني : انصرف , وهو ظاهر قول الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r19.claim: His corruption may consist in obstructing people from the right path.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r21.claim: One explanation of ruining cultivation and offspring is captivity and killing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r22.claim: The other is misguidance that ultimately leads to captivity and killing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r22.anchor: والثاني : بالضلال الذي يؤول إلى السبي والقتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r23.claim: The clause may mean that God does not love the people who cause corruption.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r24.claim: Some say it means that God does not praise or commend corruption.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r24.anchor: وقال بعضهم لا يمدح الفساد , ولا يثني عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r25.claim: It may mean that God does not approve of corruption as a religion or legal way.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r25.anchor: وقيل أنه لا يحب كونه دينا وشرعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r26.claim: Another possibility is that God does not love the practice of corruption.

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r4.claim: When he leaves or disappears, this violent man pursues sins and corruption on earth.
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r4.anchor: يعنى إذا توارى وكان رجلا مانعا جريئا على القتل

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r5.claim: Muqatil glosses the phrase as destroying every creature and reports that al-Akhnas burned a Muslim’s grain stack at Taif and killed his riding animal.
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r5.anchor: يعنى كل دابة، وذلك أنه عمد إلى كديس بالطائف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r1.claim: Tawallā means turning away from the Prophet and going off after softening his speech.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r1.anchor: عنك وذهب بعد إلانه القول واحلاء المطنق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r2.claim: Al-Akhnas acted against Thaqīf after a dispute with them: he raided at night, killed their livestock, and burned their crops.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r2.anchor: كما فعل بثقيف فإنه كان بينه وبينهم خصومة فبيتهم ليلا وأهلك مواشيهم وأحرق زروعهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r3.claim: Al-ḥarth and al-nasl mean crops and livestock; the verse may describe destructive conduct by a ruler as well as al-Akhnas’s raid.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r3.anchor: أى الزرع والحيوان أو إذا كان واليا فعل ما يفعله ولاة السوء من الفساد فى الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r4.claim: Another explanation says he displays injustice until God withholds rain as a consequence, destroying crops and livestock.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#3/r4.anchor: وقيل يظهر الظلم حتى يمنع الله بشؤم ظلمه القطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل

BURSEVI:v1p265/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r1.claim: Tawallā may mean turning away from the Prophet's assembly or gaining dominance and becoming a ruler.

BURSEVI:v1p265/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r2.claim: Saʿy is brisk walking, and by extension energetic effort in work or earning; saying 'in the earth' signals extensive corruption wherever he goes, since the encompassing setting implies encompassing action.
BURSEVI:v1p265/r2.anchor: السعي سير سريع بالأقدام وقد يستعار

BURSEVI:v1p265/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r3.claim: Ihlāk means wasting or destroying; ḥarth is crops, and nasl is offspring of animal species, with both verbal nouns used here for what is produced.
BURSEVI:v1p265/r3.anchor: ما خرج من كل أنثى من أجناس الحيوان

BURSEVI:v1p265/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r4.claim: The phrase 'to corrupt therein' gives the purpose of his striving.

BURSEVI:v1p265/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r5.claim: The destruction may recall al-Akhnas's night attack on Thaqīf, which ruined their livestock and crops out of enmity, or the killings, dispossession, and oppression of corrupt governors.

BURSEVI:v1p265/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r6.claim: A report says God placed blessing in crops and offspring when creating the means of subsistence, making their destruction the height of corruption.
BURSEVI:v1p265/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث "لما خلق الله تعالى أسباب المعيشة

BURSEVI:v1p265/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r7.claim: A report describes a governor brought to judgment and cast on Hell's bridge: the obedient pass, while the disobedient break it and fall into Hell, a journey of fifty years.

BURSEVI:v1p265/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r8.claim: God disapproves of corruption, hates it, and is angry with whoever engages in it.
BURSEVI:v1p265/r8.anchor: أي : لا يرتضيه ويبغضه ويغضب على من

BURSEVI:v1p265/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265/r9.claim: God's creating things is not corruption: corruption is removing something from a praiseworthy state without sound purpose; what seems corrupt from our perspective is, in the divine view, wholly right and good.
BURSEVI:v1p265/r9.anchor: وما نراه من فعله ونظنه بظاهره فسادا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r1.speaker: ابن جريج وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj and others take both verbs as actions of the heart: he turns away in anger and pride, then schemes to bring calamity on Islam and its people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r1.anchor: و «سعى» أي سعى بحيلته وإرادته الدوائر على الإسلام وأهله عن ابن جريج وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others take both verbs physically: he leaves Muhammad, walks on foot, waylays travelers, and spreads corruption; either kind of striving is corrupt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r2.anchor: وقيل: هما فعل الشخص فيجيء «تولى» بمعنى أدبر وذهب عنك يا محمد. و «سعى» أي بقدميه فقطع الطريق وأفسدها عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r3.claim: Saʿā can mean running, working, or earning; striving for one's family means working for their benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r3.anchor: يقال: سعى الرجل يسعى سعيا، أي عدا، وكذلك إذا عمل وكسب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r4.claim: The verb يهلك is coordinated with ليفسد.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ويهلك } عطف على ليفسد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r5.speaker: أبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r5.claim: Ubayy reads the conjunction with an added lām: وليهلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada read the verb in the nominative; it is parsed as coordinated with يعجبك, with سعى in sense, or as an independent clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة «ويهلك» بالرفع وفي رفعه أقوال: يكون معطوفا على «يعجبك».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r7.claim: Abu Hatim parses the nominative verb as coordinated with سعى, understood to mean he strives and destroys.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: هو معطوف على «سعى» لأن معناه يسعى ويهلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq takes the nominative verb as an independent clause: and he destroys.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r9.speaker: ابن كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir is reported to read with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on kāf, with harvest and offspring nominative; the same reading is attributed to Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu Haywa, Ibn Muhaysin, and transmitted from Abu Amr.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r9.anchor: وروي عن ابن كثير «ويهلك» بفتح الياء وضم الكاف، «الحرث والنسل» مرفوعان بيهلك وهي قراءة الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r10.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r10.claim: Some read يهلك with fatḥa on both yāʾ and lām, with al-ḥarth nominative, following the dialect pattern of halaka yahluk.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r10.anchor: وقرأ قوم «ويهلك» بفتح الياء واللام، ورفع الحرث لغة هلك يهلك مثل ركن يركن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r11.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r11.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the referent as al-Akhnas, who burned crops and killed donkeys.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r11.anchor: والمعني في الآية الأخنس في إحراقه الزرع وقتله الحمر، قاله الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r12.speaker: غيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r12.claim: Another commentator says the warning became general: anyone who acts like al-Akhnas deserves that curse and punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r12.anchor: قال غيره: ولكنها صارت عامة لجميع الناس، فمن عمل مثل عمله استوجب تلك اللعنة والعقوبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r13.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r13.claim: Some scholars say killing a donkey or burning a grain stack merits blame and lasting disgrace.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r13.anchor: قال بعض العلماء: إن من يقتل حمارا أو يحرق كدسا استوجب الملامة، ولحقه الشين إلى يوم القيامة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r14.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r14.claim: Mujahid interprets the destruction as God withholding rain from a wicked oppressor, thereby destroying crops and offspring.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المراد أن الظالم يفسد في الأرض فيمسك الله المطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r15.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj says harvest means women and offspring means children: hypocrisy divides the community and causes fighting that destroys people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r15.anchor: وقيل: الحرث النساء، والنسل الأولاد وهذا لأن النفاق يؤدي إلى تفريق الكلمة ووقوع القتال، وفيه هلاك الخلق قال معناه الزجاج.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r16.claim: Striving swiftly across the land is an image for stirring discord and inciting people against one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r16.anchor: والسعي في الأرض المشي بسرعة وهذه عبارة عن إيقاع الفتنة والتضريب بين الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r17.claim: A hadith warns that if people see a wrongdoer and do not restrain him, God may soon extend punishment to them all.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205/r17.anchor: إن الناس إذا رأوا الظالم ولم يأخذوا على يديه أوشك أن يعمهم الله بعقاب من عنده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r1.claim: Al-ḥarth literally relates to breaking or plowing ground and also means earning, crops, cultivation, and study; al-Jawhari also records uses for exhausting a camel and stirring a fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r1.anchor: الحرث في اللغة: الشق ومنه المحراث لما يشق به الأرض. والحرث: كسب المال وجمعه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r2.claim: Al-nasl is what each female gives birth to; its root suggests coming out or falling, as with hair and feathers, and the two verses describe people rushing forth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r2.anchor: والنسل: ما خرج من كل أنثى من ولد. وأصله الخروج والسقوط ومنه نسل الشعر، وريش الطائر، والمستقبل ينسل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r3.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r3.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses tansalu for slipping or coming away, illustrating the root of nasl.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r3.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: فسلي ثيابي من ثيابك تنسل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the verse supports cultivating fields and trees and seeking animal offspring, means by which human life is sustained; this counters those who reject practical means.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r4.anchor: قلت: ودلت الآية على الحرث وزراعة الأرض، وغرسها بالأشجار حملا على الزرع، وطلب النسل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r5.speaker: العباس بن الفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r5.claim: Al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl defines corruption as ruin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r5.anchor: قال العباس بن الفضل: الفساد هو الخراب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r6.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib says clipping dirhams is corruption on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: قطع الدراهم من الفساد في الأرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r7.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r7.claim: Ata relates that the Prophet ordered Ata ibn Munabbih to remove a tunic worn in consecration; Qatada had heard it should be torn, but Ata cited God's dislike of corruption.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r7.anchor: وقال عطاء: إن رجلا كان يقال له عطاء بن منبه أحرم في جبة فأمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ينزعها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the general sense: God dislikes every kind of corruption involving land, property, or religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r8.anchor: والآية بعمومها تعم كل فساد كان في أرض أو مال أو دين، وهو الصحيح إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r9.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r9.claim: One interpretation limits the meaning to corruption among the people of righteousness or to corruption as a religion; another says God does not command it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:205#2/r9.anchor: قيل: معنى لا يحب الفساد أي لا يحبه من أهل الصلاح، أو لا يحبه دينا. ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى لا يأمر به

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.claim: The descriptions encourage sound conduct in hearts and limbs and remind people that God cannot be kept unaware of their inner affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.anchor: والغرض بكل ذلك أن يبعث العباد على الطريقة الحسنة فيما يتصل بأفعال القلوب والجوارح

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.speaker: الرواية الأولى
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.claim: One report identifies al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, an ally of Banū Zuhra, who professed Islam, claimed love for the Prophet, then burned a Muslim’s crops and killed livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.anchor: فالرواية الأولى : أنها نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي ، وهو حليف لبني زهرة أقبل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.claim: The five traits do not prove hypocrisy: each can also characterize a show-off or another sinner; hypocrites are included, but not every person described must be one.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.anchor: فثبت أنا متى حملنا الآية على الموصوف بهذه الصفات الخمسة دخل فيها المنافق والمرائي

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r12.claim: Even a Muslim may turn away and engage in corruption, so this action alone does not prove hypocrisy.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r12.anchor: والمسلم الذي يكون مفسدا قد يكون كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r11.claim: The hypocrite speaks sweetly, invokes God as witness, and argues fiercely, while his heart conceals the opposite of his speech.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r11.anchor: كل ما ذكره باللسان فقلبه منطو على ضد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r12.claim: One account says al-Akhnas professed love for the Prophet and intent to believe, then after leaving burned Muslim crops and killed donkeys.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r12.anchor: فلما خرج من عنده مر بزرع للمسلمين فأحرق الزرع وقتل الحمر

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r13.claim: Another account says that after Badr al-Akhnas attacked Banū Zuhra at night over a feud with Thaqīf, destroying livestock and crops.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r13.anchor: مر ببني زهرة وكان بينه وبين ثقيف خصومة فبيتهم ليلا وأهلك مواشيهم وأحرق زرعهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.claim: A second sense of corruption is spreading doubts among Muslims and devising ways to strengthen unbelief after leaving the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.anchor: يشتغل بإدخال الشبه في قلوب المسلمين

RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.claim: Religious corruption divides people, severs kinship, and leads to bloodshed; 47:22 describes turning away from religion with those consequences.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.anchor: لأنه يوقع الاختلاف بين الناس ويفرق كلمتهم ويؤدي إلى أن يتبرأ بعضهم من بعض

RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.claim: Rāzī prefers corruption as spreading doubts because destroying crops and progeny is a distinct, subsequent evil rather than a restatement of corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.anchor: حمل الفساد على هذا أولى من حمله على التخريب والنهب

RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes تولى as becoming a ruler who acts like corrupt rulers, destroying crops and offspring.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.anchor: وإذا صار واليا فعل ما يفعله ولاة السوء من الفساد في الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r5.claim: Some say an unjust ruler's oppression prevents rain by divine retribution, so crops and progeny perish.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r5.anchor: يظهر الظلم حتى يمنع الله بشؤم ظلمه القطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل

RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r6.claim: The first reading fits the passage better: he professes affection in the Prophet's presence, then seeks discord and corruption when absent.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r6.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب إلى نظم الآية ، لأن المقصود بيان نفاقه

RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r7.claim: Here saʿā means striving to provoke fighting; though it originally means walking quickly, it is metaphorical for stirring conflict and destruction among people.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170#2/r7.anchor: وأصل السعي هو المشي بسرعة ولكنه مستعار لإيقاع الفتنة

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r1.speaker: من فسر الفساد بالتخريب
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r1.claim: On the physical-destruction reading, the verse first states corruption generally, then specifies it as destroying crops and offspring.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r1.anchor: ثم ذكره ثانيا على سبيل التفصيل

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r2.claim: On the doubt-spreading reading, false religion begins with doubts and proceeds to evil deeds; Rāzī calls this interpretation preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r2.anchor: ولا شك في أن هذا التفسير أولى

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r3.claim: In the report that al-Akhnas burned Muslim crops and killed donkeys, al-ḥarth means cultivated crops and al-nasl means the donkeys.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r3.anchor: المراد بالحرث الزرع ، وبالنسل تلك الحمر

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r4.claim: Al-ḥarth is what is cultivated, extending to everything plowed and planted among the kinds of vegetation; it can also mean plowing itself.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r4.anchor: وهو يقع على كل ما يحرث ويرزع من أصناف النبات

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r5.claim: Al-nasl means offspring and derives from emergence or falling out, like shed feathers, camel fur, or donkey hair; people are Adam's descendants.

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r6.claim: The root idea of nasl is خروج, and offspring are called nasl because the child emerges from the father's back and mother's womb.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r6.anchor: النسل الولد لخروجه من ظهر الأب وبطن الأم وسقوطه

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r7.claim: For the reported night attack on a Thaqīf group, exegetes offer different referents for al-ḥarth.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r7.anchor: أن الأخنس بيت على قوم ثقيف

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r8.claim: On that account, al-ḥarth may mean women, by analogy with wives being a field for their husbands.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r8.anchor: المراد بالحرث : إما النسوان لقوله تعالى : { نساؤكم حرث لكم }

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r9.speaker: قوم من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r9.claim: Alternatively, some exegetes take al-ḥarth as men, because men plow the land of reproduction.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r9.anchor: أو الرجال وهو قول قوم من المفسرين

RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171/r10.claim: Under the account of the attack on Thaqīf, al-nasl refers to the children.

RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.claim: Whichever interpretation is chosen, the phrase describes the greatest possible corruption: destroying plants and animals, or destroying animal life at its roots and branches.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.anchor: إهلاك النبات والحيوان ، وعلى التفسير الثاني : إهلاك الحيوان بأصله وفرعه

RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.claim: The compact phrase is especially eloquent, using few words to convey extreme destruction and emphasis.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.anchor: من الألفاظ الفصيحة جدا الدالة مع اختصارها على المبالغة الكثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.claim: Rāzī compares this concise expression with other brief Qur'anic descriptions of Paradise's pleasures and the earth's water and pasture.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r3.anchor: ونظيره في الاختصار ما قاله في صفة الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r4.claim: If destruction is coordinated with saʿā, the verse states the aim of his striving, not that destruction occurred; as an independent clause it states actual destruction, but the first syntax is preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r4.anchor: والأول أولى ، وإن كانت الأخبار المذكورة

RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r5.claim: Some read the verb actively with the crops and offspring as its subject, meaning that they perish.

RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ya-hlak with fatḥa on the lām, a dialectal pattern like abā ya'bā.

RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r7.claim: A passive reading of يهلك is also transmitted from al-Ḥasan.
RAZI-FULL:v5p171#2/r7.anchor: وروي عنه { ويهلك } على البناء للمفعول

RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that love means will: 24:19 uses love for wishing indecency to spread, and hatred is presented as love's opposite.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r1.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة على أن الله تعالى لا يريد القبائح بقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r2.speaker: الرسول عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r2.claim: A report says God loved worship without associating anything with Him and sincere counsel to rulers, and disliked gossip, wasting wealth, and excessive questions; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r2.anchor: نقل عن الرسول عليه السلام أنه قال : ( إن الله أحب لكم ثلاثا

RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r3.claim: If love is will, the verse means God does not will corruption, like 40:31; the Muʿtazilites infer that the described corruption occurred without His will and was not created by Him.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r3.anchor: فدل على أن ذلك الواقع وقع لا بإرادة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r4.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r4.claim: Rāzī's Ashʿarite colleagues answer in two ways: love means praise and exaltation rather than will, or, even if love means will, the definite article does not make the statement universal.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r4.anchor: والأصحاب أجابوا عنه بوجهين الأول : أن المحبة غير الإرادة

RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r5.claim: Human capacity and motives are apt for good and evil; if evil is preferred without a cause there is no Creator, while a determining cause must come from God or entail an infinite regress, so God determines the preference for evil.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r5.anchor: إن وقع لا لعلة لزم نفي الصانع

RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172/r6.claim: Since God knows corruption will occur, willing it not to occur would amount to willing His own knowledge to become ignorance, which is impossible.
